raised 16 september, from david's question: a woman naturalised out of lourenço marques would have a file naming her parents, wouldn't she? the record class is real and this archive has never tested it. a south african naturalisation memorial asks for date and place of birth, the father's name and nationality, the date and ship of arrival, and the wife and children by name and age. and the father's file would be better than hers — it names every child, so it would give her parents and her siblings in one document, which nothing this archive has tried can do. but the law may have removed her own file before it existed. an alien woman who married a british subject before 2 september 1949 acquired his nationality automatically; the south african citizenship act 44 of 1949 ended that and required an alien wife to naturalise like a man. ivone married johannes antonie oelofse de witt on 2 february 1948, nineteen months inside the old rule. if de witt was a union national she became one by marriage and there is no file for her — and nationality acquired by marriage survived the divorce, so tpd 534/1948 does not undo it. that makes de witt's own nationality a question worth answering, because it decides whether her file can exist. the gazette has already been swept: 1930 to 1960, every year, surname figueiredo, south african issues only — no naturalisation notice, with the control test run first and passing. on /negatives/. naairs, which indexes the sab naturalisation files, was unreachable on the day. the enquiry is queued for ms xaba as q5 of request 24, framed as 'is there an index entry for the surname' rather than 'find her file'.

lizzy's own 1939 census card — sauerbaum, nnnn, and a mixed marriage

opened 20 september, and it is the single most informative document this archive has found about kurt's mother. mapping the lives, from the reichssippenamt census card of 17 may 1939, bundesarchiv r 1509. (1) her birthplace. auguste leibholz née luwinski, born 28.08.1893 in sauerbaum / rössel / ostpreussen — and this archive already knew that village, because johanna thimm of sauerbaum is kurt's great-grandmother and was used as the non-jewish east prussian control when counting berlin directory pages. lizzy was born where her grandmother came from. (2) "race": nnnn. the card recorded the ancestry of all four grandparents; n is nicht-jüdisch. four n's. the german state classified lizzy as not jewish, on its own form, in 1939. (3) "basis of persecution: collective". the term for someone persecuted as part of a household rather than for their own recorded ancestry — a mischehe. it is the standard reason jacob was not taken until 26 february 1943, the fabrikaktion. the category is on the record; the inference is not asserted. (4) and it gives jacob a place of death. the record's family block reads 'leibholz, jacob [jakob], * 08.08.1884 in szubin (schubin), † before 08.05.1945 in auschwitz'. the bundesarchiv gedenkbuch entry this archive holds says 'not documented' for both death date and death place. the place is now named. the date is not. and the question it sharpens. kurt was born in 1912, lizzy married jacob in 1924, so kurt is her son by another man and jacob was his stepfather. if lizzy was nnnn then kurt's classification as a jew — he carried the imposed name israel out of germany in 1933 — cannot have come from her. it came from the father whose surname he does not carry, and this archive has no name for that man. in data/mappingthelives-leibholz.tsv.

check:evidence failed intermittently and the '26' was never a clue — diagnosed, reproduced and fixed

diagnosed and fixed 21 september. this row recorded two red runs, on 20 and 21 september, that passed again immediately afterwards, and it noted as suspicious that both reported exactly 26 problems. the 26 is not a fingerprint. it is the display cap. the gate builds a list called problems; for silent people it appends one header line plus silent[:25]. so any failure with twenty-five or more silent people prints exactly 26, whether twenty-five people are missing or all of them. two investigations read a constant and inferred a deterministic subset from what was arithmetic. reproduced. pointed at an empty dist the gate printed the signature exactly: 183 silent, capped to 25 names, 'fail check-evidence — 26 problem(s); evidence is not reaching the page'. astro clears dist before it rewrites it, so a second build against the same tree empties the directory under a gate that is mid-read, and every documented person goes silent at once. that is the mechanism this row suspected and could not show. the load-average-267 measurement is consistent with it and remains a circumstance rather than proof of which read lost. what was changed, and all four branches are tested. (1) the gate now snapshots dist — every html path with its size and mtime — before and after reading, and if the two differ it says 'site/dist changed while this gate was reading it' and refuses to judge. proved by touching a dist page mid-read. (2) an empty dist is named as such — 'holds no html at all, that is not a finished build' — instead of being blamed on the evidence. (3) if more than half the documented people are absent at once the gate says 'that is a broken or partial build, not an evidence fault' and prints how many html pages it actually read. a real evidence regression touches a handful; it does not silence a hundred. proved against a one-page dist: '179 of 187 documented people are absent from dist at once, having read 1 html page(s)'. (4) the failure line now reports the true number of silent people rather than the length of a capped list, and says '... and n more, not listed' when it truncates. the standing rule in this row still holds and is now enforced rather than remembered: never run two builds against one tree. the difference is that the gate now tells you that is what happened instead of accusing the data.

new 29 september 2026, from the landesarchiv's own letter. the sammelakte to the schöneberg ii marriage register exists and holds “nur die aufgebotsunterlagen aus dem jahre 1923” — the banns papers. a german banns file of 1923 normally contains the birth certificates of both parties, and a birth certificate names the parents. the 1924 marriage entry named no parents — the 1920s prussian form cites the birth register instead — so joachim luwinski, johanna née thimm, sally leibholz and friederike née schmul are still unconfirmed on one document, and this box is the nearest thing to one. not digitised, so no scan; copies are ordered through the digitaler antrag at service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/352800/. this is a purchase and it is david's to make. drafted, not ordered. and a clean negative so nobody orders it for the wrong reason: the sammelakte holds no divorce papers. the judgment is landgericht berlin 251. r. 80. 40 and it lives, if it lives, in a court series. second candidate on the same logic: auguste's own birth entry, groß-bössau 1893 nr. 88, which the marriage entry cites and which this archive had no way to ask for until today.

drafted 29 september 2026 as requests/39-reply-to-landesarchiv-oberle.txt. not sent — i draft letters, i do not send them. it does four things. (1) it supplies standesamt berlin viii, geburtsregister 1912, nr. 963 with the reasoning, which is exactly what frau oberle wrote that she lacked, and says plainly that the failure was ours and not hers. the move to luwinski.defranceski.com — done 12 october 2026, and the window was effectively zero

a peer session is moving the estate onto subdomains and sent a recipe. the work is done and sits unmerged on claude/subdomain-step4. do not merge it while the pages cname is null. measured 12 october: gh api repos/daviddef/theluwinski/pages --jq .cname returns null, so the site is served at daviddef.github.io/theluwinski and base must stay '/theluwinski'. pushing the branch now would make every link root-relative on a host that serves the site from a subdirectory — the exact breakage described below, self-inflicted. the order is: david says go, the peer binds at the moment of the push, not before. what the branch contains, and three of the five are not in the peer's recipe: site/public/cname; astro.config site and base; the four redirect targets (/letters pointed at /theluwinski/errands/ and would have 301'd into a 404); base.astro's origin constant, which is the trap of being out of the kit ring — the siblings read their origin from archives.json via socialhead and this archive is deliberately not in that file, so the origin is a local constant and a scratch build caught it still reading daviddef.github.io while base and every link were already right; and a link that was never a link, sources.json carrying <a href={'/theluwinski/negatives/'} inside a json string so it rendered as a literal href={'...'} and has been dead on the live site all along. the lesson, which cost three working sites across the estate: the recipe said binding first costs nothing because github keeps serving the previous build. it does — from a host where that build's own paths do not exist. binding 301-redirects the project url to the bound domain, so it moves every visitor onto a site whose base no longer matches. luwinski, falco and mazza were all taken down this way (89, 308 and 205 dead hrefs) until measured and unbound. the gap is not eliminated by reordering, it is only moved: landing config before binding breaks the site and binding before config breaks it too, whenever base is not '/'. the only fix is to make the two simultaneous. two measured facts to check after any future binding: public/cname does not bind a domain — the api can read cname null with the file sitting in the deployed output; it only stops a later deploy tearing an existing binding off. and https_enforced can be false with the certificate approved, leaving plain http serving 200 instead of redirecting, so every page has two addresses; ours is already true, measured. and the ring stays seven: luwinski is not in kit/data/archives.json, removed 16 september at david's instruction because the luwinskis are not a branch of the same family, and the peer's step zero would have put it back. case (b): this archive does not use the kit ring at all. done. david said “push”; the branch was merged at eb1e914 and a peer session bound the domain the moment the run completed. measured twice, a minute apart, and by the corrected method — every root-relative link the live page emits, fetched verbatim, rather than paths constructed from what ought to be there. home page: 40 distinct emitted links, all resolve. /leibholz/: 49, all resolve. the only non-200 in either sweep was //gc.zgo.at/count.js, which is protocol-relative and external — an artefact of my own script prefixing it with our host, not a broken link; gc.zgo.at/count.js answers 200. https 200 with clean tls on both passes, plain http 301s to https, cert approved, https_enforced true. and every old address 301s with its path preserved — /theluwinski/tree/, /leibholz/, /errands/, /dna/ all land on the same page at the new origin, so no link anyone has ever shared is lost. the four redirect stubs follow to 200. the tls risk was real and untestable and did not bite. the plan was to lower https_enforced before binding and raise it after; github refuses — put returns 404 “the certificate does not exist yet”, so that lever does not exist and nobody should design around it. we went in with no way to de-risk it, said so, and set an abort condition the peer could act on without consulting us. on a rebind of a previously bound hostname the certificate came back approved within seconds. not generalised to a first bind of a never-bound name: one data point, on a hostname that had held a cert hours earlier. and the rule we both had wrong, now settled by comparing two archives bound seconds apart: the window is not bind-versus-push, it is the distance between the bind and the deploy landing, whichever order they fall in. ours paid nothing because the deploy had already completed when the bind landed. falco was bound three seconds before its run started and was 404 for 87 seconds. so the trigger is bind after the run completes, not when it leaves the queue.

blocks: 23 corrections, each carrying what the family record said, what this archive says instead, and the evidence

where a named source overrides the family record, the correction is applied to the register and listed here with the evidence. nothing is silently rewritten: the original value is carried through as was, so a reader can always see what the family believed and why this archive disagrees.
kurt israel luwinski · died
now 15 december 1968
how johannesburg chevrah kadisha burial register: died 15.12.1968, buried 16.12.1968, westpark block l grave 211, yahrzeit 24 kislev 5729 — which is itself 15 december 1968.

now not documented; deported to auschwitz 26 february 1943
how bundesarchiv gedenkbuch en1100957, which records the deportation and deliberately gives no date of death.
morris isaac salkow · died
how johannesburg chevrah kadisha burial register: died 08.11.1991, buried 10.11.1991, westpark block u grave 2469.
gertrud leibke · husband
how census of 17 may 1939 via mapping the lives: gertrud and oskar share an address, waghäuseler str. 9/10 wilmersdorf. georg was at michaelkirchstr. 26, mitte, with lydia née perl.
georg leibholz · brother of jacob
was son of sally leibholz and friederike schmul
now not a brother — the dates forbid it. probably a cousin or nephew of the same family

how jacob was born at schubin on 8 august 1884 and georg at hammerstein on 7 june 1884 — sixty-two days apart. two sons of one mother cannot be. both dates are the bundesarchiv's, independently of the family, and that arithmetic is what this correction rests on. the wording before 20 september 2026 also said 'two hundred kilometres apart' and called georg 'a different leibholz family'. both are withdrawn. sally leibholz, jacob's own father, was born at hammerstein on 7 july 1847 and married at szubin on 24 december 1874 (corrected 27 september 2026 from 24 november, which was the family record's date and is not the register's). the family had people in both towns, so the distance between them is not evidence of anything and the surname at hammerstein is not a stranger's. what the dates rule out is brotherhood; what they leave standing is a cousin or a nephew in the town sally came from. the leibholz page has said exactly that in its 'a likelier reading' panel since the start — 'right surname, right family, wrong generation' — and this correction contradicted it. it no longer does.
ivone mota figueiredo — and a correction this archive made to the family record, now withdrawn · marriage to da rocha, before 1941 — the tree was right and this archive was wrong

was this entry formerly read: "marriage to unknown da rocha, before 1941 · was: married · now: no such marriage — she was a spinster in february 1948", sourced from the germiston duplicate original marriage register no. 34 of 1948, column 5 personal status: spinster. on that basis the ivone page published "she had never been married", "it did not happen", and "there is no marriage record to find, because there was no marriage".

now withdrawn 27 september 2026. the marriage happened and the family tree had it right. ivone married frederico pinto da rocha on 18 november 1939 at the 1.ª conservatória do registo civil de lourenço marques, and that marriage was dissolved by divorce, by a sentence of 6 december 1945. both facts are averbamentos on her own birth registration. she was therefore not a spinster at germiston in february 1948 but a divorcée of two years, and the portuguese state still recorded her as divorciado on her death certificate in 2010.

how assento de nascimento n.º 447-d, fls. 224, conservatória dos registos centrais, lisboa, 7 may 1987, transcribed from the 1.ª conservatória do registo civil de lourenço marques; averbamentos 1 and 2. photographed from the family's own papers and supplied on 27 september 2026. why the germiston register lost: it records what was declared in a south african office about a status acquired in another colony, while the assento is the continuously maintained register of her own civil status, naming a husband, an office, a wedding date and a court sentence. a divorcée declaring herself single abroad is ordinary; a registrar inventing all four is not. the lesson is the cost: this archive struck a true fact out of the family record on one word in one column, and then built three panels on the strike. working in data/ivone-assento-nascimento-1922.tsv.
kurt israel luwinski · occupation
now dress designer (1933); shop keeper (1948)
how johannesburg marriage register no. 858 of 1948, column 6: shop keeper. the 1933 emigration record gives dress designer. both are true of one man.
johannes antonie oelofse de witt · died
was no date; sasolburg
now 2 april 1963, sasolburg

how the tree's own duplicate, not an outside record. the harvest holds this man twice: 9500005, born december 1923 at johannesburg, with a death place and no date; and 9500160, listed as his son, of exactly the same name, born circa 1923 at pretoria, died 2 april 1963 at sasolburg. a father cannot be born in the same year as his son, and the two die in the same small free state town. they are one man, and the date of death is on the duplicate. independent confirmation obtained, 20 september 2026, and it did not need the estate files. "south africa, civil death registration, 1953-1967" — entry for johannes antonie oelofse de witt, 2 april 1963, sasolburg, orange free state, aged 40, born 1923 at pretoria (familysearch ark:/61903/1:1:dd9y-plt2). a national death register says what the tree's uncited duplicate said. it also settles which half of the duplicate was right about the birthplace — pretoria, not johannesburg. and it raises a doubt about the birth date: the death register makes him 40 on 2 april 1963, and a second marriage found the same day — to elsie marie geyer on 25 february 1950 (ark 1:1:6zhr-nvyn) — makes him 27 then. the two ranges overlap at april 1922 to february 1923, and the tree's "december 1923" falls outside both. declared ages are not proof; two of them thirteen years apart, agreeing against the same date, are worth recording. see data/dewitt-confirmed.tsv.
johannes antonie oelofse de witt (the younger) · identity
was son of johannes antonie oelofse de witt, born circa 1923 at pretoria
now not a second person — the same man as 9500005, duplicated

how same name, same birth year as his supposed father, same place of death, and a father-son relationship that is arithmetically impossible. the duplication also invented a wife for him — 'unknown de witt', 9500161, who exists only to be his mother — and gave delina de witt a half-brother who is really her father. found by tools/audit-tree.py, 20 september 2026, which flags a parent under fourteen at a child's birth. deliberately not collapsed into 9500005. the duplicates map in tools/build-register.py collapses records only where the pair shares an identical birth and death date, and says in its own comment that those are not guesses. this pair does not meet that bar: the birth places differ, johannesburg against pretoria, one birth is 'circa' and only one record carries a death. it is a strong inference and not an identity, so both records stay in the register with this correction attached to them, which is what corrections are for. 20 september 2026: the bar has been partly met and the records still stay apart. the civil death register gives the birthplace as pretoria, which is the duplicate's birthplace and not 9500005's johannesburg, so the two records now differ on a point where an outside source backs one of them. that strengthens the inference that they are one man and does not turn it into an identity, because nothing yet ties the johannesburg birth to anybody at all. both records stay in the register.
edwina ann wear, born green · placement
was a node in the family tree on the front page, flagged “removed — she was nobody”
now off the tree. kept in the evidence layer and nowhere else

how david's direction, 20 september 2026: “if this person is a nobody she really doesnt need to be in the tree. keep it in evidence but not on the main screen.” he is right and the panel was self-indulgent. edwina ann wear was born edwina ann green and married bruce wallace wear — leonard's younger brother — in 1980. she is a wear by marriage and no blood relation to derrick at all. this archive had spent a day on her, decided she was a coincidence, and then left her standing in the tree across all three columns under a heading announcing that she had been removed. a withdrawal does not need a monument, and a family tree is for the family. what survives and where: her burial at west park on 8 july 2014 in the cemetery-register table on the leonard page; the cancelled estate request 33157/2014 on the status page; the negative in data/negatives.json that uses her to bound the johannesburg cemetery search; the reasoning on the dna page; and bruce's own 1980 marriage on his timeline, because that is a fact about bruce. one thing changed with her. the phyllis agnes robertson node existed to explain edwina's mother. it now points where it always should have — at gillian agnes louisa nel, born wear, born eleven months into that marriage and carrying agnes in her own name.
manfred joachim luwinski · how the family left germany in 1965
was flew from berlin to melbourne — this archive's own reading, published 20 september 2026
now sailed from bremerhaven to melbourne on the ship flavia, arriving 17 september 1965

how naa: a2559, 1965/86/85-88, item id 5435314 — the australian half of the same nominal roll, whose title states the ship, the port and the date. the error came from reading the mode of travel off the arolsen folder heading, “transport by airplane”, instead of off the sheet. a folder heading describes the folder.
sauerbaum, kreis rössel — the place, on this archive's own map · where the atlas put it
was 54.35 n, 21.15 e — a pin placed before the village had been identified, and fifty kilometres from the village
now 53.935 n, 20.846 e — zerbuń, gmina jeziorany, powiat olsztyński

how german wikipedia's coordinates for zerbuń, the village this archive identified as sauerbaum on 20 september 2026. checked because a different claim was being verified — the distance from sauerbaum to bischofstein — and the arithmetic came out at 33 km against a published 15. the distance claim was near enough (17.8 km from the real village). the pin was not. the map had been showing auguste luwinski's birthplace fifty kilometres from where she was born, since before the village was identified at all.
erna, of streitstraße 39 in spandau — published as the last leibholz in the berlin books · her surname

was leibholz. read from the ocr text layer of the 1980-81 berlin telephone book, which prints "leibholz erna 3 35 84 05 20 stteitsu.39", and published as the last appearance of the leibholz name in the post-war berlin run.
now leipholz — the eighth spelling. the 1975-76 and 1979-80 telephone books print the same woman, the same address and the same telephone number 3 35 84 05, with the p clear in both.

how zlb berlin, berliner telefonbuch 15849358_1975-76 p.1444, 15849358_1979-80 p.1704 and 15849358_1980-81 p.1770, read 21 september 2026. what actually proved it was not a better scan but the alphabet either side of her. in every volume where the name is genuinely leibholz it is printed between leibfried and leibich. in the 1980-81 volume that line sits between leipert werner and leipner bodo. leipholz belongs in that gap and leibholz cannot be in it, so the surrounding names settle the letter that the ocr could not. the same technique — read the alphabet, not the word — is what found erna frida else leipholz in the schöneberg death index the same afternoon.

it mattered beyond one letter. the claim it supported was that a leibholz survived in berlin until 1981, which was this archive's latest trace of the name in the city. that trace belongs to the other spelling, and the correction makes the two ernas visible: erna frida else leipholz died on 13 january 1975, and erna leipholz of streitstraße 39 is in the telephone book for six years afterwards. two women of the same name, which the misreading had hidden inside one.
elli leibholz, married struzik, born 7 november 1915 — a surname-index entry whose death the family record could only bound · died

was "after may 13 1942". the family record gives a floor and not a date, and the register turned that floor into a year: year() takes the first four digits it finds, so the page carried 1942 as though it were the year she died, with nothing to say it was a bound.
now may 1942, at kulmhof (chełmno) extermination camp. day not recorded.

how bundesarchiv gedenkbuch entry en1169257, read 22 september 2026: elli struzik née leibholz, born 07.11.1915 in berlin, of berlin (mitte), deported from berlin to the litzmannstadt (łódź) ghetto on 1 november 1941 and from there to kulmhof on 13 may 1942; place of death kulmhof, date of death 00.05.1942. the birth date matches the family record to the day, which is what identifies her.

it explains the family record rather than contradicting it. "after may 13 1942" is not a guess — it is the deportation date, the last day anybody knew she was alive, written down as the only honest thing that could be said. the gedenkbuch closes the gap by a fortnight and names the place. the year on the page does not change and that is the point: this archive was right by accident, because a floor and the truth happened to fall in the same year. joachim luwinski's "before 1955" has no such luck behind it and is still only a bound, which the bloodline and the timeline now say in words.
hilde leibholz of wiesbadener straße 57 — and which woman is the last of the name in the post-war berlin telephone books · who is last, not the spelling

was "erna — 1980-81 telephone book — the last leibholz in the run", and, in the summary line of the same file, "then erna alone in 1980". the spelling half of this was already corrected on 21 september as 9500904 — she is a leipholz — but two things were left standing: data/berlin-postwar-luwinski.tsv and the leibholz page were never amended to match 9500904, so a reader of either still met the old surname; and nobody had asked who the last leibholz actually was.

now hilde leibholz, at wiesbadener straße 57, is the last of the name in the post-war berlin run. she is in nine consecutive telephone volumes, 1972-73 to 1980-81, in the flat felix held before her — including the very 1980-81 volume from which erna was called the last. erna is in that volume too, three places further on in the alphabet, under the other spelling.

how zlb berlin telephone books, pi_anchor 15849358, read at the alphabetical slot on 22-23 september 2026 rather than by name search, which is what turned hilde up: five of the eleven readable volumes mangle one or other of these surnames and a name search misses them. supersedes nothing in 9500904, which stands; this records the claim that was built on top of it. working in data/leipholz-telephone-slot-audit.tsv.
jaques leibholz & co., the family's konfektion firm in berlin w8 — jacob leibholz's own business · street
was kronenstrasse 59-60, published on the leibholz page, in data/berlin-adressbuch-names.tsv, in data/jacob-leibholz-deportation.tsv and in two research-log entries.
now krausenstrasse 59-60. the house number is unchanged.

how berliner adressbuch, zlb berlin. four readings in three volumes, none of which says kronen: 1925 page 1871 prints it cleanly, "jaqueb leibholz & co, konfektion, w8, krausenstr. 69. 00"; 1934 page 1462 "w8 kraufen-/strasse 69. 60"; 1938 page 1633 in the householder run "w8 krausen-/strasse 59. 60"; and 1938 page 3385, a different section of the same volume, "leibholz j & co w8 kraujeuilr 69. 60". the deciding evidence is the ocr artefact rather than the spelling: the f of "kraufen" and the j of "kraujeu" are both this scanner's rendering of the long s, and kronenstrasse has no s in that position. found on 22 september while sweeping the householder runs for row 260, and the wrong street survived because both streets are real and both sit in the konfektion quarter around hausvogteiplatz.
jacob leibholz at lutherstraße 34 in 1913 — which registry office could hold anything of his · registry office
was "so jacob's 1913 registry office is one of standesamt charlottenburg i to iv", published on kurt's page and in the research log.
now one of charlottenburg i, ii or iii. charlottenburg iv did not exist in 1913 — its earliest volume of any kind is 1922 — and the unnumbered office closes in 1897.

how landesarchiv berlin, labsa, 23 september 2026. the error came from guessing the office names rather than enumerating them, which is the same root as this archive's 143-against-207 miscount of the charlottenburg holdings the day before: the search matches an office name exactly, and the list of names is only available from the form's own autocomplete endpoint. the three surviving candidates hold 114 name-index volumes between them. working in data/labsa-charlottenburg-inventory.tsv and data/labsa-berlin-catalogue.tsv.
henrique figueiredo pinto da rocha, ivone's elder son, born 11 march 1941 at lourenço marques · the circumstances of his birth, and what his surname means

was "henrique was born on 11 march 1941 to an unmarried mother... his father gave him a surname and, on the evidence of that surname, acknowledged him. ivone did not marry him." the page also concluded that his birth registration was "the only document likely to name his father — there is no marriage record to find, because there was no marriage."

now he was born inside a marriage — sixteen months after his parents' wedding of 18 november 1939 and four years before their divorce. he carries pinto da rocha because his parents were married to each other when he was born, which is a simpler explanation than acknowledgement by surname. his father has a forename: frederico pinto da rocha. there is also a marriage record to find, at the 1.ª conservatória do registo civil de lourenço marques, 18 november 1939.

how averbamentos 1 and 2 to assento de nascimento n.º 447-d. not a proof of paternity: a husband at the date of birth is a legal presumption, not a certificate, and nothing here excludes another father. what it removes is the archive's reason for treating his surname as evidence of acknowledgement, and it replaces one unlocated document with two.
ivone mota (or mata) de figueiredo · born
was 1924, from the family tree, and repeated on her page as the heading "lourenço marques, 1924".

how assento de nascimento n.º 447-d, conservatória dos registos centrais, lisboa — "dia quatro, mês março, ano mil novecentos e vinte e dois" — and independently her 2010 death certificate, which carries 04/03/1922 in its own boxes. her own declared ages contradict each other and both: 22 at germiston in february 1948 and 24 in june 1948, when she was 25 and 26.

a living person is now named, with a town and a country, and nothing more documented

did the estate-wide standard for living people, ruled on 16 october 2026, is adopted here. a living person is named, with their relationship to the people around them and their town and country, and nothing else: no date of any kind, no record, no photograph, no structured data. ten people the source flags as living were omitted entirely and are now in the register, the blood-relatives chart and the family drawn on their relatives' pages, by name; one has a town and a country, one a country only, and eight no place, because the source records a birthplace for two of them and nothing else that belongs to the person. two of the ten are placeholder records the source names “unknown”. the test for who is living is unchanged, and derrick is unchanged: named with his parents, not even a town. the rule is applied where the register is generated, not in the templates, and the source's life spans on the edges that point at a living person are replaced by the word living. and the gate was inverted, not loosened. check:living used to fail if a living name appeared anywhere; it now fails if one appears with a year, a date, a born or died word, a field beyond name on a chart node, json-ld, a page that can be indexed, or a register record carrying anything but name, relationship and place, and it refuses rather than passes if it cannot recognise a single living person in the build. tools/selftest-living.py plants a fault for each rule in a copy of the build and a control beside it, 54 cases, and ci runs it. three known limits are written in the gate: a person recorded under one name, and the placeholders, cannot be recognised in running text; a maiden-name form is held by the digests only; and the “stands with a name” test is about layout, not meaning.
mary appleyard has a death, and the mary burch candidates are thinner than they looked documented

did mary appleyard died in january 1822. the aldenham burial register enters mary, wife of william hawkins, on 30 january 1822, aged 41, from aldenham gate, so she was born about 1780 or 1781; and the marriage entry of 5 may 1800, which this archive had not seen, writes her appleyard as the banns do. her husband william was buried on 23 november 1848 aged 76, and the widower of 65 at round bush in 1841 is him. a daughter mary had been buried in 1820, aged 7. all of it is matched by name, age and abode. her baptism is still not found, and the one yorkshire mary baptised in the right year is a coincidence of dates and not a lead. the two mary birch candidates for mary burch are weaker: a mary birch aged 16 was buried at abbots langley in 1796, who may be the girl baptised there in 1782, and a mary birch married james beech at watford in 1804, who may be the watford girl of 1782. either would exclude the candidate; neither is proved; and mary burch's origin is no better known than before. the larkin couple's daughter mary married william bilby by banns on 22 october 1843 and was widowed in october 1844, which confirms her as the mary bilby of the 1851 household and does not name her father.
the two larkin couples were told apart by their burials, and mary burch married as barch documented

did three more findmypast reads, and a free freereg one, finished the larkin question. the marriage entry of 1814 spells her barch, which is why a search for burch could not find it; they married by banns on 6 february 1814, both of aldenham, he a bachelor and she a spinster, with wm larkins and wm nicholls as witnesses, and their first child was born 52 days later. the aldenham burials carry an age and an abode, and they sort the two couples. robert, 79, from the round bush alms houses on 20 february 1859 and mary, 72, from round bush on 14 october 1855 fit the couple of the 1851 census; robert, 45, from the folly on 16 september 1832 and mary, 62, from letchmore heath on 29 february 1860 fit the widow born at edgware and her husband, and her youngest, baptised in march 1833, was born after his father died. none of the four is in the 1861 census. all of this is matching by name, age and abode, and no document ties an entry to a person. it also settles which baptism is which: the two candidate roberts, 1781 and 1789, are now two different men, and the ages favour 1781 for robert of 1814. for mary burch it narrows the birth to 1782 or 1783, and leaves two candidates, watford (a sister of whom was entered burch in 1784) and abbots langley, neither chosen. her own parents are not in the aldenham registers: a burch family appears there only from 1810. not found: the marriage of the widow's husband, in hertfordshire or middlesex indexes.
findmypast was signed in, and the larkin children turned out to be two families documented

did the surname-only searches that were left undone on 13 october were done, and what they turned up was not what was being looked for. the eleven children baptised as robert and mary larkin at aldenham are two families, not one. emma was born on 3 march 1822, only 272 days after robert william on 4 june 1821, and one mother cannot do that. a widow mary larkin, born at edgware about 1800, heads a household in 1851 with a son robert and a daughter eliza, and in 1841 with robert, joseph, eliza and thomas: she is the mother of robert william, the second joseph and thomas. the other couple is the pair of the 1814 banns, found alive in the 1851 census at aldenham as robert, 72, and mary, 69, both said to have been born there, with their daughters mary and elizabeth at home. this archive had assumed one family of eleven and explained the two josephs as a death. the assumption is withdrawn, the marks on robert william, the second joseph and thomas now say they are probably the other couple's, and emma's parents move from best candidate to probable, because the argument is a birth interval and an identification and no document names her. no mary burch was baptised in hertfordshire between 1738 and 1856, on a surname-only search of all 236 entries, and the census age of 69 points to 1781 or 1782, so the marys baptised birch at abbots langley, watford, northchurch and wigginton in those years are the candidates and none is chosen. no mary appleyard was baptised in the county before 1851, and no mary hawkins of her age is indexed at aldenham in 1841 or 1851. the findmypast burial set for hertfordshire stops about 1810, so a missing burial after that proves nothing. two smaller closings came from the free index: emma hawkins's marriage to john hull is q2 1894 at st albans, both names on 3a p758, and martha maud castle's birth is registered in q3 1895 at hitchin.
the titmus line: the probable parents of mary titmus, from a licence of 1684 and a will of 1722, and what the gaps in the free registers hide documented

did if john wright was the son of george wright and mary titmus, then mary titmus was probably the daughter of william titmus, yeoman, of stevenage, and mary harvey. the hertfordshire archives index has a marriage licence of 1684 for william titmus and mary harvey, both of stevenage, three and a half years before mary titmus was born (about december 1687, from her burial at 81 in 1769), and a will of 1722 for william titmus, yeoman, of stevenage. that is a candidate, and it depends on a lean. john's parentage is two candidates and a labourer's trade, and nothing in either document says mary wright was william titmus's daughter. a william titmus also married elizabeth clerke at wallington in 1679, who may be the same man widowed. the titmus and wright families married each other at ardeley more than once, in 1706, 1708 and 1714, so a titmus was already a wright's relation by 1708. the control searches are the finding: freereg has no stevenage baptisms for 1684 to 1690 and almost no stevenage burials for 1720 to 1723, even for common surnames, so that mary's baptism and william's burial are not found does not mean they are not there. the will of 1722 could name a daughter mary wright.
john and sarah wright of stevenage: two candidate fathers, one lean, and a marriage that is not in the index documented

did sarah wright, wife of john wright, labourer, was buried at stevenage on 27 april 1770 aged 53, so she was born about 1716 and john was a labourer. there are two johns baptised at stevenage in the right years. one, in 1717, was the son of george wright, a labourer, and mary titmus, who married at ardeley in 1708; the other, in 1719/20, was the son of robert wright, a butcher and publican whose will of 1753 is indexed at hertfordshire archives, and mary hurst, who married at stevenage in 1717. the labourer's trade leans to george's son, and that is all it does. neither john was buried young. the marriage of john and sarah is not in the index although the stevenage register is covered for those years, and a john wright and sarah bottoms who married at ampthill in 1739 were ruled out, because a couple of those names had children at ampthill in the same years as the stevenage baptisms. sarah's maiden name and baptism are not found. the will of robert wright senior (1753) could settle which john, and a copy costs £11.45.
esther wright was found again, remarried as a widow under another name, and traced to stevenage documented

did esther phillips, widow, married william harwood at weston on 3 october 1795, two years after the burial of william phillips, yeoman, and a hester harwood was buried at weston on 2 october 1831 aged 75. the forename in the burial is hester, and the only esther or hester wright in the hertfordshire baptism index for 1738 to 1766 is hester wright, baptised at stevenage on 27 december 1754 to john and sarah wright, so she is the probable esther of 1775, 20 years old and married by licence, which a bride under 21 needed a parent to consent to. the family at stevenage: elizabeth (1741), john (1742, buried a week after baptism), mary (1744), a second john (1747), hester and jane (1757). that is a match by forename, date and age, and no document names her parents. john wright's own baptism is two candidates, 1717 to george and mary or 1719/20 to robert and mary, and the marriage of john and sarah was not found. the wrights of the hertfordshire archives index at weston (george 1670, thomas 1692, ann 1693/4) are an older family and nothing joins them to esther. the hides are not family: a hide witnessed four weston weddings in these families, 1763 to 1804, and is probably the parish clerk, which corrects the line above that left the question open.
william and esther phillips were found by their marriage of 1775, under a spelling the first search did not use documented

did william philips and esther wright married at weston on 21 february 1775, by licence, both of weston. they are the parents of james phillips (baptised 1776) and ann phillips (1783), who are the cousins' grandparents of the page above. the earlier search for the marriage had returned nine william phillips weddings from 1755 to 1783 and none to an esther; it was in the index under philips, with the bride transcribed edther, and a second index, hertfordshire names online, confirmed the bride's name and added the licence. the couple and the first witness signed with a cross; a hide was a witness in 1775, and hides witnessed four weston weddings in these families between 1763 and 1804, which marks them out as the parish clerks and not as relations. william, yeoman, was buried at weston in october 1793. his parents are not found. a william phillips, yeoman, of weston made a will in 1760, indexed at hertfordshire archives and not read, and it is the likeliest place to find them; the other candidate, a william philips baptised at baldock in 1746 to charles and elizabeth, is weaker. for esther, a hester wright baptised at stevenage in 1754 is the only esther or hester wright in the index for those years, and it is no more than possible. no burial for esther was found under five spellings. a maintenance order of 1804 names a william phillips of knebworth, who is another man. the free routes now end here: the next steps are the will (£11.45 for a copy, free to view at hertfordshire archives) and the licence bond.
joseph wallis and sarah field turn out to have been second cousins, and the weston registers carry their grandparents documented

did the four parents now have pages: william wallis and mary foster, william field and elizabeth phillips. william wallis's mother, ann phillips, and elizabeth phillips's father, james, were baptised at weston to the same couple, william and esther phillips, in 1783 and 1776; and a daughter born to ann in 1810 was named esther philips wallis, which is the clue that ties her to them. so william wallis and elizabeth phillips were first cousins and their children, joseph and sarah, second cousins. that rests on three only-candidate identifications, and it is not a certificate. beyond them: joseph wallis, probably baptised at clothall in 1783 to a joseph and a mary williamson who married there in 1771; thomas field and sarah wallduck, who married at weston in 1791 and whose first william was buried as an infant in 1798, which is why the william of 1802 is probably the one who married elizabeth phillips; and thomas foster and elizabeth south, who married at wallington in 1793 with mary the youngest of five children. william field's identification is the weakest, because his age at burial in 1879 fits the baptism he probably is not slightly better than the one he probably is. not found: the elder joseph wallis's own baptism, the baptisms of mary williamson, elizabeth south and sarah wallduck, and the marriage of william and esther phillips. the search was of freereg's weston, clothall and wallington registers.
caroline wallis's parents were traced back two generations, from free registers and a census, with findmypast signed out documented

did her father is joseph wallis, baptised at weston on 22 july 1827, and her mother sarah field, baptised there on 12 july 1829. they married at hitchin in the march quarter of 1851 and the census of 30 march has them in weston village with sarah's brother james field lodging in their house; joseph's widowed mother, mary, is in the same village with six children, three of whom were baptised to william and mary wallis. joseph's parents, william wallis and mary foster, married at weston on 10 february 1827 and sarah's, william field and elizabeth phillips, on 2 june 1823. above them are candidates only: a joseph wallis who married ann phillips at weston in 1804, the one william wallis baptised there in 1807, and a mary foster baptised at wallington in 1806. the join between each rung is a name, a parish and an age, and no certificate has been read. joseph's age drifts by up to three years across the census and the death index, and sarah's at death is two years under her baptism. the sources are freebmd, freecen and freereg, all free and none needing an account; the page of the march 1851 marriage was read whole, which is how sarah field was found on it, because the index does not name a spouse. findmypast had signed out, and no password was entered. two new person pages, joseph wallis and sarah field, and one page of evidence.
caroline wallis was found at weston, in the 1871 census under another spelling, and her birth year is 1862 after all documented

did caroline wallis was baptised at weston on 16 april 1862, daughter of joseph, a labourer, and sarah. she is in the 1871 census as caroline wallace, nine, a straw plaiter, in maiden street, weston, with joseph and sarah and eight brothers and sisters, and in the 1881 census as caroline wallis, 19 and single, in the same house. eighteen months later she married george william castle. the search that found her had no surname: the 1871 index spells the family wallace, so a search on wallis returned eleven carolines from other counties and none from hertfordshire, and this archive recorded her birth year as open on 16 october. it was not open. every document made when she was a girl says 1862, her birth was registered at hitchin in the march quarter of 1862, and the 1939 register's 1863 and her age of 48 in 1911 are each a year or more out. the unnamed wallis girl of march 1863 is another child. her parents are probably joseph and sarah wallis of weston, and her page says “probably” because the join is the name, the parish, the date and the age and no document makes it; her marriage certificate would. the page that called 28 february 1863 exact was wrong twice, and the paul letter has been rewritten again so that it does not repeat it.
the free indexes were read for the english line, and caroline wallis's birth year turned out to be open documented

did three free sites — freebmd, freecen and freereg, none needing an account — were searched for the gaps the new person pages name. george william castle's death is settled as far as an index can settle it: one george castle aged 54 died in england and wales between march 1916 and december 1917 (hitchin, q3 1917, vol 3a p607), and hitchin has no george castle death in 1916, so the 1916 on one tree has nothing behind it. the castle and wallis marriage is now an index entry, both names on hitchin 3a p567 for the last quarter of 1882. but caroline wallis's year of birth is not 1863 as this archive said. the 1939 register gives 28 february 1863 and the 1957 death index gives 1862; her age of 48 in april 1911 fits 1863 and her 56 years 4 months in 1921 fits neither, which makes this archive's earlier line that the 1921 age agreed with 1863 wrong. two hitchin births fit, a caroline in q1 1862 and an unnamed female in q1 1863, and neither is tied to her. her page now says 1862 or 1863 and marks the fact disputed. her parents are still not found: freecen has no caroline wallis, though its hertfordshire coverage is patchy and that is not a finding. george castle's death has an index entry (q4 1885, aged 46), and a james and an elizabeth giddings aged 68, dead in the first half of 1883, are candidates for the norton end couple and are not claimed. for mary burch and mary appleyard the surname-only search was done on freereg and not on findmypast: no mary burch was baptised in hertfordshire 1770 to 1800, five mary birches near aldenham are possible and none is chosen, and every mary appleyard baptised in england 1762 to 1782 in that index is in yorkshire, which says where the index finds the name and not where she was born. an earlier note here was also wrong about what was open: henry robert wear's parents were never unidentified. they are robert wear and emma hawkins, both documented.
the english line gets a page for each of its twenty ancestors documented

did until today the wear, castle, hawkins, larkin and giddins people existed on this site as paragraphs inside the tree, the wear line page and the leonard page, and nowhere as people. each of the twenty direct ancestors now has a page at /people/, from henry robert wear and martha maud castle back through three more generations to the six aldenham ancestors found on 12 and 13 october — william hawkins and mary appleyard, robert larkin and mary burch among them. each page carries the grade on the same five-word ladder the tree uses, a family chart in which every link says how it is known (read in a record, a best candidate, or a family tree's word) as a class and as a word under the name, a dated table of what is known, and a list of what is not established. eleven are graded documented and nine probable, and a person can be documented while a parent is only a best candidate; the page names which. nobody here was born after 1895, so no living-person rule is needed, and derrick's father leonard keeps his own page. the tree now links each of its entries to the people it describes. two things found by building it. the pages ratchet caps this archive at one hand-drawn shared page and people is a page name six siblings already carry, so the pages are drawn with the kit's persontree and evidence rather than exempted or the cap raised. and the kit's sibling row never reads a node's mark, so a sibling's “half-brother” or “best candidate” would have been dropped silently and left to colour; it is moved onto the dates line, which the row does print. a death year was wrong in our own data. building george william castle's page put two years side by side: the register gave 1917 and a tree's entry here gave 1916. the index says q3 1917 at hitchin, aged 54, so 1917 stands, caroline's second marriage came three years later, not four, and the home page now agrees. the same pass found the front page and kurt's page still carrying his 1933 emigration as fact; both now say he is first placed in johannesburg by july 1939. the gaps are on the pages, not here: mary appleyard and mary burch have no baptism found, and the county-wide searches for both used a forename filter that has not been redone surname-only, because the findmypast session expired and signing it back in is not this archive's to do.
two generations out of one parish register, and the census the row sent me to could never have answered it documented

did work list row 128 had asked since 16 september for the parents of john hawkins b.1820 and emma b.1822 of the red lion cottages, aldenham — derrick's great-great-grandparents through their daughter emma, who married robert wear at southwark in 1881. it nominated the 1841 and 1851 censuses. the 1841 census could never have answered it. all twenty hawkins entries for the parish were read and at twenty john was already boarding away from home, at aldenham checkers with katherine nicholls, 70, and william kimpton, 20. the row's instrument was the wrong one. so the parish registers were read instead — 141 hawkins baptisms, 44 hawkins marriages, 30 larkin marriages, every page. john hawkins, baptised aldenham 1819, son of william hawkins and mary appleyard. the only john the register offers in the window, the rest excluded on age, his whole sibling set present from 1801. and emma is emma larkin, daughter of robert larkin and mary burch — banns at aldenham 18 september 1842, both resident in the parish, the only john-and-emma pair among the 44 and falling exactly where the baptism of their eldest in 1843 said it must; then her own baptism, aldenham 1822, father robert, mother mary, the birth year matching the 1871 census to the year. appleyard and burch are surnames this archive has never held. and the nine children came out whole where there were six: robert 1843, betsey 1849, richard 1851, jane 1853, john 1856, emma 1859, mary 1861, henry 1863, alfred 1865 — the 1871 household holds six and the three missing are the three eldest after robert, which is what a household looks like when the older children have gone. held as probable and not documented, and the reason is the same for all three marriages: every one is a banns entry with an empty marriage-year field. banns are the announcement on three sundays, not the wedding; what supports each is a baptism to that couple in the same parish soon after. and each identification is best-candidate — one pair of the right names in the right window — which is weaker than a document naming the person. half a warning dissolved on the way: this archive has carried a caution about two emma hawkinses, mother and daughter, after merging them once and publishing it. the mother was never an emma hawkins at all — that was her married name. what is left is the sharper half: she appears as emma hawkins in every census of her married life, which is exactly how a woman gets filed under a name she was not born with. and two properties of the instrument, measured: this set indexes each banns calling separately so one wedding appears two or three times under different ids — counting entries is not counting marriages — and on findmypast page= is not the pagination parameter and does not fail loudly: it returns “0 results found” because an unknown parameter is treated as a filter nothing matches. it is _page=. that is the same shape as the year-filter trap already on the books: a zero that is an artefact of the query and looks exactly like an absence.
the one page the subscription had not given up, four days before it lapses documented

did the probate calendar page for george william castle the younger — martha maud's elder brother — had been recorded on 20 september as the thing that got away: iiif at 2864x4361 behind findmypast's image gateway, session-locked, a request carrying the visible cookies answering 403. david signed the session in on 12 october and it was read the same hour, in four overlapping native-resolution regions. it is worth four new facts and it corrects one of ours. the entry: “castle george william of 85 jackmans-place letchworth hertfordshire died 23 august 1939 at st. bartholomews hospital london e.c.1 administration london 2 november to margaret castle widow and cyril george castle printer. effects £1166 13s. 2d.” he did not die at letchworth, which is what this archive said. letchworth is his residence — the only thing the index gave — and the archive read it as the place of death. he died in a london hospital forty miles from jackmans-place. the thirteen-day reading is unharmed and slightly sharpened: his sister sailed from london on 10 august and he died in london on the 23rd. and the word on the page is administration, not probate — so there was no will, and he died intestate at about fifty-four; the index column had called it probate and this archive repeated it. it also names a wife nobody had. margaret castle, widow, taking the administration jointly with cyril george castle, printer — who now has an occupation and sits in the position a son ordinarily occupies, which is still not a proven relationship and is not claimed as one. and a figure that a smaller view got wrong. effects £1166 13s. 2d. a downscaled read of the same line gave “£1100 15s. 2d.” and would have been written down; did the last unclosed reading on agnes was that she died in the east. the 8 october sweep left east berlin on the argument that “a west berliner listed in a 1979 telephone book did not move to the ddr” — right, and now with a date under it: until 9 november 1989 a west berlin pensioner could not relocate east at all. so the hypothesis lives only from 1990, when she was 101, to 1994, when the index closes and she would have been 105. scoping to those years turned 605 volumes and 41.9 gb into 47 volumes and one gigabyte — the whole of east berlin, eleven offices, affordable in an afternoon. all 47 were downloaded and scored. thirty-three legible and read, fourteen blind and not read. no leibholz, no leipholz, no leipsholz, no luwinski and no kerger in any of the thirty-three — the first time her maiden name has been put to any east berlin office. and every single 1990 volume in east berlin is blind, in eleven separate offices — every office in east berlin — all at 0.000, while the 1991 volumes of the same offices score 1.4 to 2.5. that is a scanning boundary at 1990/91 and it is the third this archive has measured — kreuzberg's text layer begins at 1963, schöneberg's at 1984, east berlin's at 1991. a date where a series changes scan generation is a property of the digitisation and not of the records; it differs per office and has to be measured every time. prenzlauer berg proves the per-office part: it is blind for 1990, 1991, 1992 and 1993, and only 1994 reads. two of the eleven boroughs stop at 1990 regardless — treptow and hohenschönhausen have no 1991-94 index in labsa at all, which is a holding limit and cannot be closed by reading. the fourteen blind volumes are named and are not being read, and that is a judgement recorded as one. 1,759 pages, perhaps fourteen l-block reads, against a prior that requires a woman of 100 to leave the borough she had lived in for decades, cross a border that had been shut her whole adult life and open for weeks, and die in the east within five years — and an l-block reading would carry exactly the narrowness this archive spent the same morning writing a caution about. scoped and named so anyone who disagrees can do it in an afternoon. one kerger came out and she is not agnes: “kerger, karoline henriette lucie”, köpenick 1992, three forenames and no married name. and köpenick cross-indexes its women both ways — leibner also as wilk geb. leibner, leipner also as kirbach geb. leipner — which is the behaviour spandau did not show for else hedwig herfert the same day. cross-indexing is an office's habit and not a rule, now observed in two directions rather than assumed in one. so agnes reduces to two readings and neither is reachable today: she died outside berlin, with no address to start from, or after 1994 and behind the thirty-year closure.

with auguste and siegfried, and nobody knew what happened in between. and the first thing to say is that i rediscovered half of it. the leibholz page has carried the 1939 teil iv entry for this house for a fortnight, with the owner read as gertrud eisenberg née haake and spier h. identified as hans spier, born 2 december 1894. the work list row still described the question as open and nobody had read the row against the page that answered it. and that admission was itself wrong within the hour: the 1941 entry is on the same page too, quoted in full since 21 september, owner's sara and all. the first check stopped at the panel that matched the search term and the answer was in the panel after it. what is genuinely new is three volumes — 1940, 1942 and 1943 — and two of them answer a question the page posed in writing. the 21 september panel ends: “the 1942 and 1943 volumes would close it further, and the text layer will not give them up … those two pages have to be found by eye.” they have been. the house is 2 and 4 together on a corner, cross-referenced to barbarossastraße 36a, so the transport list's number and the directory's are one door. and the owner goes from a name, to a name plus the name the state imposed, to nobody. 1939: “e eisenberg, g., ww.” 1940 and 1941: “e eisenberg, g. sara, ww.” 1942 and 1943: “e ungenannt.” the compulsory middle name dates her as jewish on the state's own record — the decree took effect on 1 january 1939, which is exactly why the 1939 volume, compiled from 1938 returns, does not carry it and the 1940 one does. what “ungenannt” means is not proved and this archive does not pretend. it is consistent with a forced sale, with administration, with her death and with an editorial gap. what is recorded is that the house jacob was deported from had a named jewish owner in the 1941 volume and no owner at all in the 1942 one, and that one tenant — kephan, h. israel, einrichter — leaves at the same boundary. spier carries no “israel” in any of the four years while the same page marks two others and the same volume marks four men in one house round the corner, so the absence is evidence and not silence. not claimed: that spier hid him or sheltered him. forced relocation into designated rooms was ordinary administration in berlin by 1942 and “b/spier” records an address, not a kindness. and a negative from yesterday is explained rather than overturned: a full-text sweep had found spier and treuchtlinger co-occurring only at page level, which was right — the street page does not contain the string “treuchtlinger” at all, because the heading ocrs as “tremhtliagrr str.” a search for both terms could never have found it. what works is walking the running heads, which survive the ocr far better than the body.

closed — spandau p rep. 480 nr. 2458, blind at 0.03 — and it is recorded as unread rather than quietly counted as a negative.
derrick had kurt’s own papers in a drawer, and one of them puts a date of ours in doubt documented

did derrick photographed kurt’s documents and sent them. a berlin driving licence and its international permit, 1934, and a german passport issued at johannesburg in 1939 — all eight pages now published with a line-by-line german transcription and an english translation beside each. the licence contradicts a year this archive has printed everywhere. “ausgestellt für herrn kurt luwinski, geboren am 11.5.1912 zu berlin, wohnhaft in bln.-schöneberg, meraner strasse 2 … berlin, den 30. januar 1934”, class 3, four reichsmarks of prussian fee stamps on it. the family tree says he emigrated in 1933 and this archive repeated it as fact on the home page, the atlas, the dna page, derrick’s page and his own. a man who had emigrated in 1933 did not take out a berlin licence from a schöneberg address in january 1934. either the tree’s year is wrong or he left and came back; the paper cannot say which and the archive is not choosing. the withdrawal is registered and check-superseded found eleven places still asserting it, every one corrected. and it exposed something worse and quieter: the earliest document this archive holds placing kurt in south africa is the 1939 passport. everything before that was the tree. the licence also moves the family into meraner strasse five years early — the census of 17 may 1939 was the earliest the archive could put jacob, auguste and siegfried in that flat, and the son was living in it in january 1934. and the passport answers an open question outright. kurt’s page has asked for weeks where “israel” came from, reasoning that he left before the decree and as a mischling was outside it anyway. the german consulate in johannesburg applied it to him on 26 july 1939 and he signed it himself: “israel kurt luwinski”, in his own hand, under a consular stamp with an eagle and a swastika. what is not answered is why a consulate treated him as a jew rather than a mischling; the question is not closed, it is sharper, because it is now about an act by a named office on a known day. one more thing the passport closes: beruf, hutmacher. the archive had auguste a milliner, samuel selling hüte en gros, and kurt buying the piccadilly hat company in 1941 — but kurt’s own stated trade was “dress designer” in 1933 and 1956, so the hats looked like something he picked up in johannesburg. he was a hatter in 1939, two years before he bought the shop. and the ehefrau and kinder columns are struck through, which agrees with the 1948 register calling him a bachelor. and the thing that is not a fact at all: three photographs of him. twenty-one and smiling in profile; the same man in sepia; and twenty-seven at a consular counter in 1939, the year his father had four left. this archive has written about him for weeks out of register numbers and gazette notices. derrick has had his face all along.
the home page had been contradicting a correction for nine days, and a reader found it withdrawn

did david looked at the grandparents block on the front page and asked whether it was right. it was not, in two places, and one of them was this archive’s own published correction being ignored by its own spine. georg was listed under “jacob’s brothers”. the leibholz page has said since 20 september that he cannot be one: jacob born at schubin on 8 august 1884, georg at hammerstein on 7 june 1884, sixty-two days apart and one mother, both dates from the bundesarchiv. cousin is the strong reading. the spine went on naming him a brother, and counting “all four brothers” where there are three, for nine days. the correction existed; nothing had ever read the spine against it. and the second error was made worse by yesterday’s own finding. the block said auguste “survived the war in berlin”. survival is documented — she died at kraichtal in 1975. berlin is not: the support is a census card of 17 may 1939 and a 1940 directory entry this archive itself says may not be her, the directory sweep records her absent from 1941, and her second husband died at sommerfeld in january 1946. the framing rested on her being ‘the catholic wife of a deported jewish husband’ — and the divorce of 21 march 1940, published here yesterday, means she was his ex-wife by nearly three years. which broke a load-bearing explanation elsewhere. mappingthelives-leibholz.tsv reasons from the 1939 census card that the mischehe ‘is the standard explanation for why jacob was not deported until 26 february 1943’. a protection that ended in march 1940 cannot explain a survival until february 1943. that row was saved by its own last sentence — ‘the archive states the category, which is on the record, and not the inference that follows from it’ — which is exactly why it was right not to have made the inference. what survives the new date is a different reading: 26 february 1943 is the eve of the fabrikaktion, which seized jewish forced labourers, and gertrud — registered as an arbeiterin — died on the morning of the 27th. forced labour rather than marriage. labelled a hypothesis, because no document says where jacob worked. and my withdrawal string was too greedy for the third time today: a bare ‘four brothers’ matched ‘twenty-four brothers’ on the register page, about a different family and true. narrowed. the lesson is now three for three and belongs in the tool’s own docstring, not just in mine.
an archivist spent a morning explaining something that was sitting unsent in our drafts folder documented

did the landesarchiv berlin answered, and the answer is three documents and a lesson. arabella oberle sent, free of charge, gertrud leibholz’s death entry (standesamt wedding 1943 nr. 1291, p rep. 830 nr. 114) and both sheets of the 1924 leibholz–luwinski marriage (schöneberg ii nr. 6, p rep. 161 nr. 171 — note the index this archive had been citing is nr. 271, a different volume). all three are now published with a line-by-line german transcription and an english translation beside them. what the marriage entry settles: the divorce — landgericht berlin 251. r. 80. 40, final 21 march 1940 — which is the third of three possibilities this archive listed for the 1940 directory’s “auguste leibholz, witwe” and refused to choose between. the contradiction is gone and the word is not: a divorced woman is not a widow, and the volume was compiled before the decree was final. it also gives auguste’s birth register citation, groß-bössau 1893 nr. 88, after weeks of sweeping the ermland on a village name; samuel leibholz standing as witness, which is the first document putting him beside jacob; and a floor of 21 march 1940 under the fricke remarriage. and it breaks a prediction this archive published in advance. on 20 september, holding only the index, it wrote that the entry would name both sets of parents. it names no parents at all — the 1920s prussian form cites each party’s birth register instead. second time in one day that a row here was planned around a field the relevant form revision does not have; the other was bt 27 in a different century and a different country. the gate built for this caught two more places and i made it cry wolf twice. check-superseded found the claim still standing in twenty-alone.tsv and berlin-namensverzeichnisse.tsv — both real, both corrected. it also flagged two statements that are true, about the 1874 schubin entry and a 1940 johannesburg certificate, because the string i withdrew was the sentence pattern rather than the claim. the 1874 form does name both sets of parents and this archive proved it. a withdrawn value must be specific to the claim or the gate starts refusing correct work. narrowed twice before it passed. and the worst thing in the letter is ours. she could not find kurt’s birth: the 1912 registers are not digitised and she needs the responsible standesamt — “die bloße angabe berlin reicht nicht”. this archive established it on 20 september: standesamt berlin viii, geburtsregister 1912, nr. 963, luwinski · kurt myszislaus. a reply saying exactly that has been sitting in a drafts folder for nine days, because a direct send was refused by permission mode — correctly, and it was not worked around — and then nobody told david it was waiting. an archivist did unpaid work teaching a method this archive had already used, on the same day the draft was written. and she gave us something we did not know existed: the sammelakte survives and holds the 1923 aufgebot papers, which normally contain both parties’ birth certificates — so the four parent names the marriage entry failed to give may be in a box in berlin. not digitised, orderable for a fee, and that is a purchase and david’s to make.

did record atlas asked whether the bt 27 finding holds for other year ranges. checking it was housekeeping and it turned into evidence. three eras sampled: 1907 has no last-uk-address column at all and buckets ages by nationality; 1937 and 1939 are the same form, p.m. 21, columns (1)-(9); a 1951 piece is a typed us military transport manifest filed inside bt 27 with none of the board of trade form left. the series is not homogeneous and the era has to be checked before a row is planned around a field. the 1937 half of that answer was the one that mattered here. it meant leonard's own windsor castle sheet of 12 march 1937 carries column (6) — so it was opened, and it reads “wear, mr l a r · 20 · 18, ridge avenue, letchworth, herts. · engineer”. three departures across twenty-nine months — leonard in march 1937, his father in april 1939, his mother and the four youngest in august — all giving the same house. this morning’s correction rested on two entries four months apart; it now rests on three across more than two years, and “the family’s own house” is no longer an inference from two departures but a fact about where they lived. it also settles a word. both 1939 entries abbreviate to “18 ridge ave” with a flourish and this archive published the reading with a query against it; leonard’s clerk wrote ridge avenue out in full, with the county. and it does not do the other thing. the move out of 72 pix road is still bracketed 1921 to october 1935 from the pix road side. what is new is the far end: settled at ridge avenue by 12 march 1937, so the gap is at most seventeen months, and the 1936 and 1937 electoral registers would close it. the lesson is not about letchworth. a holdings question from somebody else’s map, answered properly instead of guessed at, handed back a record this archive had owned since 16 september and never opened.

did leonard's page said janette was “a cinema cashier in lodgings on ridge avenue, half a mile away”, and the worklist row was titled “the 1939 register finds her in letchworth lodgings”. the 1939 register says no such thing. it gives an address — 18 ridge avenue — and an occupation, and nothing about tenure. the archive knew the family house as 72 pix road, inferred that a different address must be a room she had taken, and wrote the inference down as a fact. the passenger lists took it back, and they had been in the archive since 16 september. bt 27 column (6), last address in the united kingdom, is not in the findmypast transcript and exists only on the page image. it reads 18 ridge ave, letchworth for henry robert on the durban castle of 5 april 1939, and again — one brace over all five — for martha maud and the four youngest on the dunvegan castle of 10 august. it was the family’s own house. she had not moved out; she was alone in the house her father left in april and her mother left in august. the transcript had been read and the image had not, which is the same fault as reading one line of importer output and not opening the file it described — twice in one day. and the row’s own question turned out to be unanswerable by this record set. the row wanted a letchworth neighbour aboard, to explain why south africa. bt 27 in 1939 stops at “country of intended future permanent residence” — a country and nothing finer, no destination address at all — so no amount of reading these lists says where in south africa anyone was going. two pages were read in full and twenty-four were not, and the row says so instead of implying a voyage-wide negative: no hertfordshire address on durban castle p6, one on dunvegan castle p7 (roundwood lane, harpenden) sitting immediately below the wear brace. a passenger list is written in booking order. adjacency is not acquaintance, and it is recorded as a fact and not as a connection. also settled from the image: they entered s africa as intended permanent residence, so they sailed as emigrants rather than on a passage out and back; and his occupation is machine minder in a clear hand where the index has “machine minister”. one method note for whoever is next: the findmypast viewer’s image endpoint speaks iiif, so a single column can be cropped and read at native resolution. region crops are refused on any page the viewer has not opened. that is an access control, it was not worked around, and it is why twenty-four pages stayed shut.

did ivone’s first husband now has a date of death in the register — 2 april 1963 at sasolburg — carried as a was/now correction with its reasoning attached, because the source is the tree’s own duplicate and not an outside record. the duplicate itself gets a second correction saying it is not a second person. what it did not get is collapsing. the duplicates map in build-register.py takes records only where the pair shares an identical birth and death date, and says in its own comment that those are not guesses. this pair does not meet that bar — johannesburg against pretoria, one birth “circa”, only one death recorded. widening a rule quietly to fit a case is how the two emma hawkinses happened. both records stay visible with the correction on them.
