did fifty-nine cited facts across three hosts. arolsen: seven citations, all seven pointing at one document, and only one of the seven is supported by it. familysearch: forty-six, and only two are wrong. naairs: six, none verifiable — they are urls with session tokens and the service has not answered since 16 september. the first pass said thirty-three familysearch citations were wrong. it was counting parish registers: the record is the baptism or the burial and the tree correctly holds the birth or the death — stanilaus born 27 september 1810 and baptised 14 october, valentin dead on 12 july 1878 and buried on the 15th. twenty-five of the thirty-three were that. the two that are real are one error made twice: ivone’s and johannes de witt’s marriage of 2 february 1948 both cite the record of kurt and ivone’s marriage of 19 june 1948. the right record was already in hand from three days ago.
a man the tree has twice, and the duplicate was carrying his death documented

did the same audit checked 164 people by arithmetic alone and found three impossibilities. two are martha schuenke, dead in 1930 with sons born 1933 and 1940. the third pays for the whole exercise. johannes antonie oelofse de witt, born december 1923 at johannesburg, has a son of the same name born circa 1923 at pretoria — a father aged nought — and both men die at sasolburg. they are one man. and the duplicate carries a fact the original lacks: death 2 april 1963. so ivone’s first husband died at sasolburg on 2 april 1963, aged thirty-nine, and the date was sitting inside a duplicate nobody had looked at. the split also invented a phantom wife and a spurious half-sister.
a citation that cannot be falsified from its own text is not much of a citation inferred

did the reason the familysearch citations are 44 out of 46 sound and the arolsen ones are 1 out of 7 is not that one archive is better than the other. it is that a familysearch citation carries the record’s own description in its text — “entry for x and y, 19 jun 1948” — so a wrong one announces itself without anything being opened. an arolsen citation is a bare url. there is nothing in it to check against, which is exactly why six wrong ones survived in a tree that is otherwise careful. the audit is now a tool, tools/audit-tree.py, so it can be re-run rather than remembered.
an arolsen index entry is a pointer, not a fact withdrawn

did four documents were opened with the consent and two of them show the tree has misattached a record, both in the same shape. alfred, born 9.9.1917, is made a father of children born in 1933 and 1940; his card says polish, catholic, farm labourer, single, sachsenhausen, dead in july 1942 at twenty-four. felix, born 19.2.1923, is given a birthplace of grafenau, germany; his document gives no birthplace at all — it is a form 11 return of the landrat grafenau dated 19 august 1946, an allied listing of foreigners in the american zone, and its nationality field reads russland. the place of registration has become the place of birth. the rule follows, and this archive should apply it to itself first: an index entry gives a name, a date of birth and a docid, and everything else is on the document. the 191 leibholz index entries recorded here without opening anything are pointers, and the file now says so.
the man the tree calls a father died at sachsenhausen, single, at twenty-four withdrawn

did the tree makes alfred luwinski, born 9 september 1917, the father of manfred and joachim — and cites an arolsen record as its source. that record was opened. it is a registration card of the berlin office for the registration of war victims, and every field contradicts the tree: geburtsort a polish place, beruf landwirt, religion kath., nationalität poln., familienstand ledig — single — inhaftiert sachsenhausen, and “† 11.7.42 15:20, herz- und kreislaufschwäche”, which is the standard camp formula and is not a cause of death. the reverse gives his home: przasnysz, piłsudskiego 117. a polish catholic farm labourer who never married and died at twenty-four. he is not the father of anybody born in 1933. the tree cites this exact card for manfred’s 1933 birth and for martha schuenke’s 1930 death, and it contains neither fact and neither person. manfred and joachim’s father is unknown; the only candidate left is the alfred luwinski who was a bügler and a head of household at putbusser straße 24 in 1933.
a branch of this family flew from berlin to australia in 1965 documented

did the consent declaration was ticked and the emigration file opened. it is an intergovernmental committee for european migration nominal roll, headed melbourne, marked “australian government financially assisted”, stamped september 1965, filed under “emigrations — transport by airplane”. four lines of it are one family: manfred luwinski, born 14.11.33, aged 32, of berlin, occupation modell fitter; helga, aged 31; and two children aged ten and three, who are living and are not named here. forwarding address: c/o mr h. marquardt, canberra act — and the tree carries helga as helga erna marquardt. her family was already in australia and brought them out. the berlin directory lines up exactly: manfred is a schlosser at egellsstraße 16, tegel, in 1957, 1959 and 1961, and vanishes after 1961. schlosser and model fitter are the same trade. he vanishes because he left the country. and the tree already knew where he ended up without knowing how: manfred joachim luwinski died at brisbane in 2012.
a generation in the tree that cannot be true as written withdrawn

did reading the tree against the documents turned up a fault in the tree. it makes alfred luwinski, born 9 september 1917, the father of manfred born 1933 and joachim born 1940 — and gives his wife, martha schuenke, a death in 1930. a father of sixteen, and a mother three years dead at the first birth. the 1933 berlin directory meets the same problem from the other side: its alfred luwinski is a bügler and a head of household, which fits a man old enough to father a child that year and not a boy of sixteen. three readings and none chosen. what would settle it is in queensland: manfred died at brisbane in 2012, and an australian death certificate names the deceased’s parents.
ruled out the one cemetery kurt is actually in withdrawn

did when this archive swept the johannesburg municipal cemetery registers it stated its bounds carefully, including that the sweep did not cover the chevrah kadisha, “a separate database — a wear would have no business in a jewish cemetery, but the exclusion is stated rather than assumed”. that is right about the wears and wrong about kurt. the family tree gives his burial as chevra kadisha, johannesburg. he was registered as a jew in germany and carried the imposed name out of it. the burial society keeps its own database, one enquiry would give a plot and usually whoever arranged the burial — and it may settle a discrepancy this archive is carrying, because the work list says he died on 15 december 1968 and the tree says 15 december 1969.
arolsen holds kurt himself, and six more of his family documented

did searching the arolsen archives for the whole surname returns nine records, and seven of them match this archive’s own register by exact date of birth. kurt is one of them — “luwinski, kurt, 05/11/1912”, docid 11214358, “1 incarceration documents / 1.2.1 deportations and transports / part 24: folder mfn01335”. that is the same docid already held for jacob and auguste, so the three of them are in one folder of five hundred documents, and his index date of birth matches the register to the day. the archive knew the docid; it did not know kurt was indexed under his own name inside it. the others sit in four different classes: felix in the allied registration of foreigners and persecutees; manfred and helga sharing a single docid in “3.1.3 emigrations — correspondence and nominal rolls”; alfred in post-war evaluations. two of the nine are people flagged living in the family tree and are not named here. everything above is the index entry: every document behind it needs a consent declaration ticked, and this archive does not tick declarations on anybody’s behalf.
two leads closed by absence, and only one of the absences means anything inferred

did oskar luwinski, the master tailor of steglitzer straße 7, is in neither arolsen nor mapping the lives. he exists in one line of one directory and in no record of nazi persecution at all — consistent with a man who was not persecuted, and one absence in two archives proves nothing. anton luwinski of deuthen is not in arolsen either, and that adds nothing: his own 1939 card already reads “race nnnn, basis of persecution unknown”, so a persecution archive should not hold him, and it does not. the two sources agree and neither takes him further. he stops being a separate lead and becomes part of the ermland case — a luwinski born twenty miles from lizzy’s village, waiting on the same undigitised films.
named the film this archive has been reading for a week without naming it inferred

did twice now a west park register page has been reached by opening images by hand, and neither time was the film written down — so every grave question started from nothing. behind the indexed collection sits catalogue record olib:4148464, two hundred and ten films of johannesburg cemetery registers, twelve of them west park private graves by year range. leonard bought grave 56045 on 13 september 1969, so folio w 8 is in film 107638608, “wpc private graves registers 1963–1970”, 488 images, and nowhere else. opened, it reads alphabetically by purchaser surname — image 401 is the t section, theunissen, tyson, terblanche, taljaard, taylor — which puts the f folios around 180 to 200. folio f 3/8 itself was not read: the viewer kept reverting to its thumbnail grid and the hunt was abandoned rather than padded out. the film number is worth more than the folio, because the folio may not even be wear’s.
found lizzy’s parish, and found that eight of its nine films are not online inferred

did a village means a parish and a parish means a register. the familysearch catalogue names it in its own words: “parish register of baptisms and deaths for gross bössau, ostpreußen, now biesowo, olsztyn, poland. also includes kunzkeim, sauerbaum, willims and kleisak (kreis rössel)” — 1690 to 1897, on nine films. eight of the nine are not digitised. the two that matter both answer “film number not found” while signed in: 7948905, taufen 1793–1890, which would hold joachim luwinski’s 1865 baptism and name his parents; and 7769256, geburten (kopie) 1881–1958, which would hold lizzy’s birth. the one film that does open was checked to the frame: at image 591 the camera photographed the title board, “gross-bössau / krs.rössel / 1798-1847 / †”. right parish, wrong years.
seventy-one luwinskis in the world and not one of them east prussian withdrawn

did with the sign-in restored, the surname was matched exactly across all of familysearch: 71 records. twenty-two west prussia, thirteen posen, two silesia, and the rest american immigration and the two south african marriages. none in east prussia — where lizzy was born. and that is a fact about the index, not the family: the ermland registers are held as catalogued film and no name index reaches them, and the full-text instrument that reads unindexed images returns, for luwinski, exactly what it returned three days ago — milwaukee and chicago naturalisations, all american. one more label to distrust: the viewer files this catholic parish under “germany, lutheran baptisms, marriages and burials”. anyone trusting it would conclude these were the wrong registers and go home.
lizzy’s own census card, and it answers three questions at once documented

did auguste leibholz née luwinski, born 28.08.1893 in sauerbaum / rössel / ostpreussen — and this archive already knew that village, because johanna thimm of sauerbaum is kurt’s great-grandmother and was used as the east prussian control when counting berlin directory pages. her card records the ancestry of all four grandparents and reads “race”: nnnn — four times nicht-jüdisch. the german state classified her as not jewish, on its own form, in 1939. and her basis of persecution is given as collective, the term for someone taken as part of a household rather than for their own recorded ancestry — a mixed marriage, which is the standard reason jacob was not seized until the fabrikaktion of 26 february 1943. the same record’s family block gives jacob a place of death the gedenkbuch leaves blank: auschwitz.
fixed the wording, and the page had already said it one paragraph further down withdrawn

did correction 5 called georg “a different leibholz family” and gave as its reason that hammerstein is “two hundred kilometres” from schubin. both are now withdrawn: sally leibholz, jacob’s own father, was born at hammerstein on 7 july 1847, so the distance is not evidence of anything and the surname there is not a stranger’s. what rules out brotherhood is the sixty-two days, not the two hundred kilometres, and the correction now rests on that alone. the leibholz page carried the same fault — “these are two leibholz families. ours is the schubin one” — one paragraph above a panel that says the opposite: “the family had people in both towns… right surname, right family, wrong generation”. the page now says in as many words what it used to claim and that it was wrong.
and the panel i had not read gave the letter its best line withdrawn

did the same panel carries the marriage date: szubin, 24 november 1874. prussian civil registration began on 1 october 1874, so the marriage is seven weeks inside it and must be an ordinary standesamt entry rather than a jewish community register. the bydgoszcz letter drafted an hour earlier had raised that boundary as an open question and asked the archive to check both. it no longer speculates — it gives the date, says which book the record should be in, and keeps the community register only as a fallback. that is the fourth time today something was raised as new that this archive already held, and the cause has not changed: i read the work list and the top of a page, and the answer was further down it.
hammerstein is not a stranger’s town, and a published correction leans on the idea that it is withdrawn

did drafting the bydgoszcz letter turned up something that cuts against this archive. correction 5 disputes georg leibholz’s brotherhood on the ground that he was born at hammerstein, west prussia, two months and two hundred kilometres from jacob at schubin in posen. the argument treats hammerstein as a place this family has nothing to do with. it is not. the front-page chart says the great-grandparents were “hammerstein · married szubin 1874”, and the letter sent to koszalin on 15 september asked for “standesamt hammerstein 1884 — georg; and sally, 1847”. sally leibholz, jacob’s own father, was born at hammerstein. the arithmetic still rules out brotherhood — two sons of one mother cannot be born two months apart — but the geography is gone from the argument. a leibholz born at hammerstein in 1884 is not a stranger sharing a surname; he is a leibholz born in the town jacob’s father came from, which is what a cousin looks like.
no east prussian index exists, which is why the thimms cannot be found inferred

did david asked what could be discovered about the thimms. all 2,500 familysearch collections were enumerated. for the prussian provinces it has indexed church records for posen — 11.6 million — silesia, pomerania, brandenburg and west prussia. for east prussia it has two: both königsberg funeral sermons, both image-only with zero indexed records, ending in 1794 and 1900. there is no east prussian church index at all. that is also the retrospective explanation for something odd found on friday — seventy-one luwinskis in the whole world and not one east prussian. it is the index that stops at the provincial border, not the family. and a join the archive already had the pieces for: johanna thimm died at zeutern in 1955, auguste died at kraichtal in 1975, and zeutern is a district of kraichtal. the page lists them as two places. mother and daughter died in the same small town twenty years apart.
friederike schmul is not in the church books, and she would not be documented

did the posen collection holds thirty-three people with that exact surname and all thirty-three were read. no friederike, no szubin 1874. what is there is jewish — wolf schmul and beila lepotke, isidor schmul and liebchen katz — including a ricke schmul, which is a diminutive of friederike, born in january 1832 and therefore fifty-two when jacob was born in 1884. right name, right province, wrong generation; written down so nobody else chases her. she is absent because those are church books and a jewish marriage is not in one. prussian civil registration began on 1 october 1874, so a szubin marriage that year is a judenregister or a standesamt entry — and either way it is at bydgoszcz, where this archive already has an acknowledged letter sitting. a prussian marriage certificate of 1874 names both sets of parents, a generation above the top of the chart.
a geneteka negative that the control destroyed withdrawn

did the polish genealogical society’s index was searched for leibholz marriages in kujawsko-pomorskie, 1860 to 1890. nothing. then the same query for kowalski — the commonest polish surname there is — and that returned nothing too. the url parameters are wrong or the search needs a posted form. the leibholz zero means nothing, is not recorded as a negative, and geneteka remains untested.
the file the consent does not reach, and the one it does inferred

did t/d 52.971, the tracing case for oskar leibholz, serves metadata and no images even with the declaration ticked — no document list, no docids, no viewer — and says why: “parts of the file are not displayed for data protection reasons. in such cases, please contact the arolsen archives.” the consent opens deportation lists and registration cards and stops at the correspondence, which is what a t/d file is. one thing the metadata does give: creation date 1949 to 2002 — somebody asked about oskar in 1949 and the file was still being added to fifty-three years later. a letter is drafted and not sent. but a different series is served without restriction: 6.3.1.1, tracing inquiries 1945–1946, which returns forty-three topics for this surname.
a woman in palestine wrote to jerusalem in may 1946 asking what had become of them documented

did jewish agency for palestine, search bureau for missing relatives, questionnaire no. 2, “location of relatives abroad”, dated 23 may 1946, file 50764. the person sought: leibholz, willi, aged 55, born at stolp in pommern, last information march 1943 from berlin, last address berlin-neukölln, lenaustrasse 25, occupation butcher. with him: erna, 48, born hammer, wife; heinz, 23, son; and ruth, 22, daughter — a child this archive did not have. the person who asked: tabori-hammer born nachum, ruth-trude, of benei-braq, palestine, born 9 september 1899 at hamburg, formerly of berlin-moabit, turmstraße 59, relationship “brother in law and his family”, signed in her own hand. the tracing service answered her through the jewish agency on 8 december 1947 and closed the case a fortnight later.
and it settles where willi was born, which this archive left open this morning documented

did the page of testimony said only “germany”, and the note written this morning said so in as many words. the 1946 form says stolp in pommern. jacob, samuel and oskar were all born at schubin in posen — two hundred and fifty miles and a different province — so the lenaustrasse leibholzes are documented as not kurt’s family rather than merely unproven, and this morning’s caution turns out to have been the right one. two hammers survived and both went looking: ruth-trude in 1946, and eva khava hammer olsher, who wrote willi’s and erna’s pages of testimony later — both through erna’s family. the honest disappointment is that the row wanted a survivor on kurt’s side, and the file that would give one is the closed one.
read corrections.json properly, and it caught two more things inferred

did after raising the chevrah kadisha as new when it was already the first entry in the file, the whole of corrections.json was read against the eighty-four open rows. two hits. first, a row plans to have morris isaac salkow’s cape town estate “ride along” with a cape town request — and correction 3 says he died and was buried in johannesburg, westpark block u grave 2469, on 8 november 1991. a better candidate for the cape file surfaced in friday’s familysearch sweep: isaac morris salkow, born 1897 in lithuania, died in the cape province on 10 october 1938, probate 1938–39. the forenames are reversed and the deaths are fifty-three years apart. nobody should order that file as ivone’s husband’s until the reference is checked against a date. second, the row blocked on the arolsen consent is now openable, and it named its own next step: a tracing case for oskar, t/d 52.971, fourteen documents — and a tracing file names the person who asked.
called jacob a stepfather, and the archive’s own record calls him the father withdrawn

did this morning’s entry reasoned that because kurt was born in 1912 and lizzy married jacob in 1924, kurt must be “her son by another man” and jacob his stepfather. that is an assumption and the source says otherwise: the family tree records jacob leibholz as kurt’s father, and work-list row 152 states the archive’s own position in the same terms. a child born twelve years before his parents marry is illegitimate, not fatherless — and that is precisely why he carried his mother’s surname while his younger brother was registered a leibholz. auguste was eighteen in may 1912 and jacob twenty-seven. the point survives and improves: if lizzy was nnnn then kurt’s classification as a jew came from his father, and the father has a name. under the 1935 laws a child of one jewish and one non-jewish parent was a mischling and did not carry the imposed name; somebody counted as a jew did. kurt was counted a jew — a question with a documentable answer rather than a loose end.
called it a persecution database, and the card said otherwise withdrawn

did an hour after writing that anton luwinski was “in a persecution database”, his record was opened. “race”: nnnn. “basis of persecution: unknown.” mapping the lives indexes surviving 1939 census supplementary cards, and being in it is not evidence of persecution. what the record does give is a birthplace: deuthen, kreis allenstein — in the ermland, about twenty miles from sauerbaum where lizzy was born. two luwinskis from two villages in the same small catholic corner of east prussia. a better reason to look than the one that was claimed, and still not a relationship.
laid the directory against the memorial database, household by household documented

did the berlin address book gives leibholz householders with trades and street numbers. mapping the lives, built on the 1939 census card, gives people with dates of birth and death at addresses — 114 of them under this surname. matched on street and house number rather than on name, they line up. “a. israel, fleischermeister, levetzowstraße 13” is alfred leibholz, born 04.12.1887, died 8 august 1942 — which is why the 1942 volume has no entry for him. and he is not alone at that address: else née seelig, died august 1943; kurt, born 1927; lieselotte, born 1923, died december 1943; marianne, born 1921. a master butcher, his wife and three children in one back-building flat. the weinstraße traveller who became a building labourer had a wife, jenny née rosenberg, dead before the war ended. the lenaustraße butcher lost erna and a son of twenty.
and the control that stops the whole reading running away with itself withdrawn

did heinrich leibholz, verwaltungsbeamter, leinestraße 32, neukölln, is in the directory every year to 1942 and gone from 1943. he died on 9 august 1948. he survived the war. so a leibholz vanishing from the berliner adressbuch does not mean a death, and the series read off the page images today — seventeen, eleven, ten, nine, six, four — cannot be read as a casualty count. it never claimed to be. now there is a named man proving why it must not be. one more caution from the same table: arthur leibholz, sanitätsrat, is printed in the 1938 volume and had died in november 1937. these books are compiled a year ahead and carry the dead for a year.
two luwinskis in the whole memorial database, and one of them is new inferred

did searching it for luwinski returns exactly two people. one is lizzy — “leibholz, auguste née luwinski, *28.08.1893, meraner str. 2”. the other is anton luwinski, born 16 october 1919, at schindekopstrasse 7, lehrwerkstatt ostpreussisches baugewerbe, königsberg — the training workshop of the east prussian building trade. this archive’s east prussia page is built on nineteenth-century parish entries; anton is the first twentieth-century luwinski found in the province, and he is in a persecution database. neither oskar the master tailor nor alfred the presser is there at all. nothing connects anton to lizzy but a surname and a province, which is a reason to look and not a relationship.
a search that turns luwinski into löwinsky, caught by opening the page withdrawn

did sweeping the berlin householder section for luwinski across 1900 to 1943 returned the name in two years: 1933 and 1909. a 1909 householder would be lizzy’s father’s generation, which this archive has never had — and a work-list row was written about him. then the page was opened. it runs “löwenthal — 1639 — löwisohn” and there is no luwinski on it at all: it is semu lowinski, dr julius lowinskis, willy lowinsky ingenieur g.m.b.h., r. lowinsky nachfolger dampf-waschanstalt. the search fuzzes lu to lo and ö. four minutes to check, and it would have taken a day to unpick.
turning that doubt on a finding already published, and finding a master tailor documented

did if the 1909 hit was a mirage, the 1933 one had to be re-verified too. it holds — page 1671 runs lutz to lux, the right alphabetical place, and the line reads “luwinski alfred bügler n31 putbusser str 24”. but directly beneath it, on the dash, is a name the text layer had hidden: “—oskar schneidermstr w35 steglitzer str 7”. oskar luwinski, a master tailor, with his own business. lost to the same convention that hid four leibholz households this morning, twice in one day. there were two luwinski households in berlin in the only year the name appears at all — a presser and a master tailor, both in the garment trade. lizzy luwinski was a dressmaker and milliner.
kurt’s mother, perhaps, in charlottenburg in 1957 inferred

did the post-war berlin volumes are not in the series this archive had been querying — that one stops at 1943 — but they exist under other identifiers, and they are set in antiqua, so the text simply reads. the 1957 namenteil, page 518: “fricke auguste rentn chlb 1 kais-friedr-str 79”. auguste fricke, a pensioner, kaiser-friedrich-strasse 79, charlottenburg. lizzy was born in august 1893 and died in june 1975, so she was sixty-four in 1957 and “rentnerin” is exactly right; she is the only auguste fricke in the berlin name sections of 1955 to 1980. a candidate and not a finding: fricke is a common north german surname and one name in one directory is how the bloom mariner went wrong. her death registration of 22 june 1975 would carry an address to compare.
separated the two kurts at last documented

did every build prints the same complaint: “kurt luwinski matches more than one register entry and is deliberately not linked” — kurt israel of johannesburg who died in 1968, and a kurt who died in 1995. the second kurt is now placed. the 1964 berlin name section gives “luwinski kurt postfacharb -21 stephan[str]” — a post office worker in moabit — and the 1970–71 telephone book gives him a number. two more of the family are there with him: manfred, a fitter, at egellsstraße 16 in tegel across 1957, 1959 and 1961, and joachim, a stove-fitter, in ramlerstraße in 1967. the register already holds manfred joachim luwinski born 1933 and joachim luwinski born 1940. the two kurts are now separated by city, trade and decade instead of by a death date alone.
published that kurt lived at the hat shop, and it was the same fact twice withdrawn

did this morning’s entry said the wholesale hatter’s address matched one of kurt’s four berlin addresses, and that a second matched oskar’s. it is circular and it is withdrawn. those four addresses are not kurt’s. they are the four leibholz households in the census of 17 may 1939 — jacob, auguste and siegfried at meraner straße 2; samuel at kommandantenstr. 29; oskar and gertrud at waghäuseler str. 9/10; georg and lydia at michaelkirchstr. 26 — carried on the atlas under a loosely worded pin. saying the directory agreed with them was saying the same thing twice, and it went into a commit message before it was checked. third correction of the day.
what the directory actually adds: four men, four trades documented

did the census gave four addresses and no occupations. the 1938 and 1939 pages give the occupations. jacob traded as jaques — “jaques kaufm schönebg meraner str 2” — and printed directly beneath him is “jaques leibholz & co, konfektion, w8 krausenstraße 59.60”, so the ready-made clothing firm this archive has been watching since 1924 is his. samuel sold hats wholesale. oskar was a kaufmann. and georg ran a laundry at michaelkirchstraße 26. none of that disturbs the argument that georg was not their brother — he was born at hammerstein, they at schubin — it just gives four men their working lives.
read the whole surname off the page images, year by year, and found the law doing its work documented

did the text layer could not read these pages and this archive said so. the iiif page images can. leibholz householders in the berlin directory: seventeen in 1938, eleven in 1939, ten in 1940, nine in 1941, six in 1942, four in 1943. but the number is not the finding. the names are. in 1940 samuel is no longer samuel — the entry reads simply “israel, hüte, kommandantenstr 29”. in 1941 two more men carry it, and both have lost their trade in a single year: a. israel leibholz of levetzowstraße 13 from fleischermeister to arbeiter, wilhelm israel leibholz of weinstraße 6 from vertreter to bauarbeiter. in 1942 every name carrying “israel” is gone. the four who survive to 1943 — a police official, a nurse, a clerk, a bank official — are exactly the four who never carried it. the directory marks them, and then loses them.
jaques leibholz, meraner straße 2, last seen in the 1939 volume inferred

did item 7 of the berlin list asked for jacob at meraner straße 2 year by year, on the reasoning that “the year he stops appearing is the year the record of his life in that city stops”. he is in the 1938 volume and the 1939 volume and no volume after. the 1936 street section lists the tenants of meraner straße 1 to 5 and no leibholz is among them, so the household arrived between 1936 and 1938. he was deported from berlin on 26 february 1943; the directory loses him three volumes before that. one entry away from him, in 1940 only, is “auguste, witwe, schöneberg, badensche straße 9” — and the archive will not join those two up, because jacob was alive until 1943 and a widow in 1940 cannot be his wife unless something happened that nobody here knows about.

did the morning’s correction was that a page count had mixed four sections of the book. the afternoon’s is worse and on the same page: in a german directory only the first entry of a run spells the surname, and every entry after it begins with a dash. searching the text for “leibholz” finds one line in ten. the file published at lunchtime said that from 1939 nothing was left under the name but a printer’s cross-reference. followed properly, the 1940 volume holds ten leibholz householders (this entry said eleven until 23 september; the eleven belongs to the 1939 volume, and the enumeration here has always listed ten) — a master butcher, a police official, a widow, a pensioner, a clerk, a bank official, the hat wholesaler and two wilhelms. what saved the published version was that it had refused to state the disappearance as a finding. the refusal was right; the description underneath it was wrong.

did the berlin address-book sweep reported leibholz page hits falling from 24 in 1933 to 2 in 1943 and read it as a surname leaving a city. a berlin volume has four sections: householders and firms, the trades index, institutions, and the street directory. in 1933, twenty-four pages carried the name and exactly one of them was the householder section. the other twenty-three were the street and trade indexes, where a single household generates a dozen hits. the count measured the size of the book as much as the size of the family, and the thimm control did not catch it because the control had the same flaw. the name section has now been read on its own, volume by volume, 1920 to 1943.

did the work list said eleven record sets. all 3,502 familysearch collections were enumerated and filtered: there are thirty-two. matching the surname exactly rather than loosely drops 16,156 rows to 111, and all 111 were read. two new records. phyllis agnes wear married robert selwyn norquoy on 14 june 1952 at malvern — which is where the defendant’s surname in wld 790/1957 comes from, a name this archive had from a court index and could not explain. and kathleen edith wear and james cecil foot, 26 may 1945, in an anglican parish register: the marriage was known from a transcription, the record was not, and it is the first documentary evidence of this family’s denomination in south africa.

did every tree loses caroline wallis after her husband died in 1916. she remarried in q3 1920 at hitchin — caroline castle to james james — and was caroline james for the last thirty-seven years of her life, which is why her death in 1957 could not be found under either of the surnames people were searching. the 1939 register has her at 38 norton road, baldock, widowed a second time, and gives her exact date of birth: 28 february 1863, not the 1862 every secondary source repeats.

did yad vashem had been used here for exactly one list. searched properly, leibholz returns 88 victim records across four collections — and jacob's record carries a field this archive never had: "details of transport: transport 30 from berlin to auschwitz birkenau, extermination camp, poland on 26/02/1943." the date has been on these pages for a fortnight. the train had not. it also gives his citizenship as germany, which matters to the statelessness argument two pages away. oskar's record closes the distance between his two deportations: berlin to theresienstadt 17 march 1943, theresienstadt to auschwitz 16 october 1944, and date of death 16 october 1944 — the same day the second transport left. and the source behind the transport number is a book this archive did not know it was standing on: not the bundesarchiv gedenkbuch cited on every page here, but the gedenkbuch berlins der jüdischen opfer des nationalsozialismus, freie universität berlin, edition hentrich, 1995 — berlin's own. it has never been consulted directly and it should be. one discrepancy settles against arolsen and in the bundesarchiv's favour: yad vashem has georg born 1884, not 1885. and one decoy is written down before it costs anybody a day — "kurt leibholz, 1927, berlin, murdered" is not our kurt, who was a luwinski, born 1912, and died in johannesburg in 1968.
three of them are on one document, and one of the three had been gone ten years documented

did the arolsen archives had sat on the sources page under "identified, not yet worked" since 14 september. worked on the 17th. the index needs no consent from anybody and it holds 213 leibholz entries. it confirms jakob 08.08.1884 schubin and oskar 13.05.1887 schubin from records with no connection to the bundesarchiv — and only those two leibholzes in the whole index are recorded as born at schubin. it carries two of the brothers under the compulsory name, leibholz israel oskar and leibholz georg israel, which puts the 1938 decree published here this morning onto the family's own paper. it holds a post-war tracing case for oskar, t/d 52.971, fourteen documents, which exists because somebody asked. and then a search for auguste returned somebody this archive did not know was in the persecution records at all: "leibholz, auguste, maiden name luwwinsky, born 28.08.1893". that is lizzy, carried here for a fortnight as 1893-1975 with no date — and the maiden name is spelt with a doubled w, a seventh form of the surname and the first that is german rather than south african. then the document identifiers were compared. jacob, auguste and kurt all resolve to docid 11214358, folder mfn01335, under deportations and transports. it is one document. the father who was deported, the mother who was not, and the son who had been in johannesburg for ten years, all three named on a single sheet. this morning it was written here that kurt was probably "named inside a document about somebody else"; by the afternoon the somebody else had a name and it was his father. what stays labelled: the shared docid is a hard fact from the index; what kind of document it is, is not, because nobody here has read it — opening one requires ticking a declaration of consent about the use of sensitive personal data, and this archive does not tick that on anybody's behalf.
a surname leaving a city, and a control that proves it is not the scanner documented

did david asked what more could be done on the leibholz and luwinski side. the whole line lived in berlin and this archive had never looked in the berlin directory. the zentral- und landesbibliothek has digitised the berliner adressbücher from 1799 to 1970 — one volume a year, six to seven thousand pages each, householders by name, trade and street — free, no account, answering a json query. 1,047 page hits for leibholz, 23 for luwinski. the first thing out of it: leibholz page hits per annual volume run 24 in 1933 and hold between 15 and 24 through the thirties — then 12 in 1940, five in 1941, six in 1942, two in 1943. and the control is not an idle one. thimm — johanna thimm of sauerbaum is kurt's own great-grandmother, east prussian and not jewish — runs 66, 53, 47, 65, 72, 68, 45, 75, 69, 63 and 75 in 1943: as common in the last volume as in the first. the scanner did not get worse, the fraktur did not get harder, the book did not get smaller. the limits go in with it and they matter more than the number: a page hit is a page and not a person, twenty-four to two is a small base, and deportation, emigration and administrative exclusion from directories all look identical in a count — jews were being struck out of german commercial listings from 1938 quite apart from being deported, and a count cannot tell those apart. and a lead: the luwinskis of berlin are in the garment trade. alfred luwinski, bügler — a presser — at putbusser straße 24 in wedding in 1933 and 1936, a lorry driver by 1943, while lizzy was a dressmaker and milliner in the same city. a brother is the obvious guess and it is a guess.
two hundred and nineteen commits citing kew, and the catalogue had never been opened documented

did david asked whether this archive had ever looked at the national archives. it had not. the pages carry rg10, rg11, rg12, rg13, rg14, rg15, bt 27, wo 329, wo 372 and wo 392 — hundreds of references to records held at kew — and every one came second-hand through a commercial index's transcript. discovery is free, needs no account and answers json. the first hour produced four things. every citation verifies, and two verify better than they were published: wo 392/15 is specifically "section 5: south africa (union defence forces)", which is exactly the claim this archive makes about leonard wear, and wo 329/1120 adds the page range 312-622. wo 372/4/50790 is the exact item reference for fred james castle's medal card, in kew's own words — "scottish rifles 10061 serjeant. scottish rifles 7815432 serjeant. machine gun corps 195568 serjeant." findmypast gave only the piece and printed the discovery id on its own transcript; this archive had it for hours and never followed it. dp/12/1/14 and dp/12/1/15 are the baldock baptism registers, 1880-1895 and 1895-1910, at hertfordshire archives — the register this archive had been gesturing at all day, now an orderable reference. and luwinski returns zero across 2,500+ british archives, filed with the reason a catalogue is not a name index. a reusable tool went in with it, tools/tna.py, because the failure here was not ignorance of the source but never having reached for it.
found him: sergeant 10061, cameronians (scottish rifles), and a career soldier into the 1920s inferred

did frederick james castle is the only castle male line this archive has and he had been missing from every english record since 1901. he is found, and the chain runs: the 1901 census has him at eleven at norton end, baldock, son of george w and caroline; the 1911 census has a frederick castle, 21, single, born herts baldock, in meeanee barracks, colchester — and the original image, read at 299 per cent, gives column 5, unit or arm of service, as scottish rifles, which the transcript leaves blank; and the campaign medal roll, tna wo 329/1120, gives fred james castle, sergeant, 10061, cameronians (scottish rifles), british war medal and victory medal. this morning the identification rested on one census age. it now rests on two matches arrived at from opposite ends — the forenames fred james, exactly as the general register office registered him in 1889, and the regiment, exactly as an enumerator wrote it over his line in 1911. and his medal index card, wo 372/4, explains every absence the row was built on: sergeant throughout, three service numbers — 10061 scottish rifles, 195568 machine gun corps, and 7815432 scottish rifles. an eight-digit number is a post-1920 issue. he was still a sergeant after the war, which is why he is in no 1921 household, no 1939 register and no english death index. not proved, and the file says so: the medal roll carries no birth date and no birthplace, so the link is forenames plus regiment and not a document stating identity. a service record would state it, because it names next of kin.
nine born, eight living, one died — and all nine are now named documented

did the 1911 census asks a married woman how many children she has borne. caroline answered nine. this archive could name seven, and the baptism register turned out to stop in 1879. it closed anyway, from the household. the 1901 census has the family whole — rg13/1298 folio 49 page 26, schedule 192, norton end, norton, baldock: george w castle 36, caroline 36 born weston, and five children including frederick, 11, and martha, 5. they had gone back to norton end, the hamlet where george william was himself raised by his giddins grandparents after his mother died; he brought his own family home to it. the ninth child is sarah ann wallis, born 19 august 1882 at weston, two months before her parents married and registered under her mother's maiden name — not a castle birth in the index at all, which is why no search for castle births could have found her. and the one who died is named: sidney charles castle, born q2 1898 at hitchin, died q4 1900 at hitchin, aged two. one entry in each index, no competitors, and he was gone five months before the 1901 census, which is why no census ever showed him. the arithmetic closes exactly. and the six-instead-of-nine was three separate indexing failures: sarah ann filed under wallis, martha maud with a blank mother's maiden name, sidney charles missing too. a filter on a field that is sometimes empty is a filter on the indexing, not on the family.
frederick castle was a soldier, which is why nobody could find him at home inferred

did he is in the 1901 census after all, aged 11 at norton end — the earlier search that came back wrong had found the other norton end castle family, three schedules away on the same night. and in 1911 there is a baldock-born frederick castle, 21, single, at meeanee barracks, colchester: rg14 piece 10304, schedule 9999, military road and mersea road. a regular soldier is not in anybody's household. the age is the discriminator and it is thin but real — 21 on 2 april 1911 means born between april 1889 and april 1890, which fits ours and excludes both of the other baldock freds. it is not proof and it is labelled probable: the entry says frederick, not frederick james, and it rests on one age and a birthplace. what it changes is the shape of the question. the 1921 census holds one baldock-born frederick castle in all england and wales and it is the other family's; ours is out of the country by 1921, is not in soldiers died, and is in no death index. a regular soldier who vanishes like that went abroad and stayed, or died in a service soldiers died does not cover.
part of this morning's withdrawal comes back, in a different record set documented

did the electoral registers were withdrawn today because the set tested — 1832 to 1932 — returns page images and indexes no elector at all. there is a second and different set, england & wales electoral registers 1910-1932, and it carries names: a search for castle in hertfordshire returns arthur frederick castle in 1929 and 1930, frederick castle in 1919 and 1920. it cannot do what the withdrawn row wanted, because it starts in 1910 and the question was bermondsey 1885 to 1900. it can place the baldock castles year by year from 1919 — the decade in which caroline became caroline james and frederick disappeared. the withdrawal stands; what was wrong was the claim about one set, not the idea.

did the first of eleven institutional letters to come back. reference o-s.6342.406.2026, signed by the head of the slupsk branch: the archive holds no registers of the german civil registry office at czarne — standesamt hammerstein, kreis schlochau — for 1874 to 1899, and no books of the jewish community there at all, and no information about what became of either or where they might now be. that last clause is what makes it a good letter rather than a brush-off. hammerstein is where georg leibholz was born on 7 june 1884, and an 1884 birth entry is the one document that would name his parents and settle whether he belongs to this family. this archive holds that he does not — jacob was born at schubin in posen on 8 august 1884, two months later and in another province — and that finding now rests on the gedenkbuch alone, because the record that could overturn it is gone. sally leibholz, born 1847, predates civil registration entirely, so only the synagogue books could have held him, and those are the ones that do not exist. acknowledged the same day, in polish, in their own thread.

did the 1911 census has caroline answering nine children born, eight living, one died, and this archive can name seven. the baptism register names both parents on every line, so it should have named all nine. all 823 castle baptisms in the hertfordshire set were sorted by mother's first name and the caroline block read: between the barbara block and the catharine block there is exactly one row. the reason is a coverage bound and not a search failure — sorted by year, the latest of 195 castle baptisms at baldock is 1879, and the children were born 1884 to 1904. martha maud's own baldock baptism of september 1895 is not in the set either. the instrument ends five years before the family starts, the two unnamed children stay unnamed, and the answer is in the parish register at hertfordshire archives rather than in anything searchable from here. the one row is worth having: ada may castle, baptised 10 april 1887 at weston, father george william castle, labourer, mother caroline. the first baptism read for any of caroline's children, and it puts the family at weston — her own birthplace, and where sarah ann wallis was born two months before the marriage.

did the harvested match-holder's tree records "ada may castle, died jul 1969, hitchin". she married in q4 1909 at hitchin, volume 3a page 1171, aged twenty-two. and the death index has no such entry: ada-anything castle born 1884 to 1890, all england and wales, returns sixteen rows, not one at hitchin and not one in 1969. a woman who married in 1909 did not die a castle sixty years later. this is the caroline james trap in miniature, and it is the second time in two days the same mechanism has hidden a woman from this archive — a tree recording a death under a maiden name its owner had long stopped using. her married surname is not guessed here: marriagefinder offers two page-mates from the index and page-mates are not a marriage. the general lesson is worth more than ada may — every married daughter in that tree with a death recorded under castle is now suspect.

did yesterday this archive filed a row saying the england and wales electoral registers had returned nine entries for william wear, surrey and london, 1885 to 1900, and called them the best unworked source for the bermondsey wears — an annual address record covering the years that bracket both brothers' deaths. today one was opened. every row in that record set says "no name on record" and carries a pdf icon: they are page images of volumes, not entries about people. searched without a place filter, william wear returns 3,478 of them in devon and durham — weare in devon, the river wear in durham. john smith returns the same nameless rows in lancashire. luwinski returns zero, and so does a nonsense string, so the fields are not inert; they simply match a place. the "surrey and london" came from a place filter typed by the same hand that then reported it as a finding. a result count is a property of a search box. this archive has now made that mistake over two giddins dna matches, over two archives-index zeroes that were three records each, and here — and it wrote the warning after the first one. what survives: the bermondsey volumes are digitised and can be read page by page for 1885 to 1900. it is an afternoon of images, not a search, and the row now says so.

did asked to check for a fault the sister archive at mazza had just been caught by — a per-person builder that never opened its own evidence files, so twelve documented people were told on their own pages that nothing had been read about them. this archive has no per-person pages, so it could not fail in that exact shape. it failed in a worse one. every file in data/ was audited against every build script: build-register.py reads the myheritage export and corrections.json, the two living-persons guards read the export and a hash file, and that is the whole list. all twenty-one .tsv evidence files — the gedenkbuch, six censuses, the 1939 register, the passenger lists, the court files, the bermondsey households — were read by nothing. their contents reached the site only where a human had retyped them into a paragraph. the clearest casualty: the register printed samuel israel leibholz's birth as "june 28 1877?", the source tree's question mark intact, while data/leibholz-gedenkbuch.tsv held bundesarchiv entry en909753 giving 28 june 1877 at schubin and his death at auschwitz on 10 april 1943. the archive had the citation and the page showed the doubt. eleven people — three blooms of yarmouth, four hawkinses of watford, two castles, gertrude wear, a letchworth lodger — were documented in the repository and appeared nowhere on the published site at all.
