did tools/build-evidence.py now reads every evidence file through an explicit manifest and writes what each record says about each person; /evidence/ publishes all 135 records about 100 people; and the register carries a record read column. tools/check-evidence.py runs on every build and refuses it three ways: a file in data/ the manifest does not declare, a stale build, or a person named in an evidence file reaching the published site with neither a record nor a correction. all four failure modes were reintroduced deliberately and all four exit 1. and it changes no date. the register and the charts still draw the export as given — the question mark on samuel's birth is still there, because that is what the source says. the record now sits beside it instead of in a file nobody reads. where a named source genuinely overrides the family record that is a correction, carried as was and now, and it is a different mechanism on purpose.
the new builder hung three divorce actions on the wrong kurt, and the fix is that it now refuses to choose withdrawn

did written in the same hour as the entry above, and caught by reading its own output. the register holds kurt luwinski, died 1995, a surname-index entry, and kurt israel luwinski, 1912 to 1968, who is the man this archive is about. the linker tested exact names first and only fell back to first-plus-last, so the index man matched exactly and won while the real one never got a vote — and wld 1950/1948, wld 497/1951 and wld 2368/1951 were attached to a stranger who outlived kurt by twenty-seven years. it now pools every candidate before deciding and links neither when more than one person answers to a name, naming both on the page so a human resolves it. a name match is not a person match. this archive has now said that about a census index, a surname-tagged dna match, three frederick castles, eighteen bermondsey wears and two emma hawkinses — and then written a script that did it anyway. the same check also turned up a duplicate the register's own collapse list does not cover: johannes antonie oelofse de witt is in the source twice, once with a death date and once without.
and the second guard caught the first one leaking documented

did the first build of the new evidence page failed check-matches: a free-text note in the match-derived castle file identifies a living dna match holder as somebody's grandson, and publishing the file published him. the builder now carries a per-file redaction list and that column never reaches the page. the guard written eight days ago, after three living people were leaked into a build, caught the tool written to fix a different problem on its first run.
followed the pix road household to the end of all four lives documented

did the pix road find opened one question worth the day: louisa shenton was henry robert wear's sister, so a descendant of hers would carry the wear half of derrick's ancestry and not the castle half — the independent test this archive has wanted since it read the segments. the answer is no. births, surname shenton, mother's maiden name wear: one result, stanley w shenton, q1 1924, hitchin. deaths, surname shenton, born 1924: the same child, q1 1924, hitchin. born and died in the same quarter, to a mother of forty-one. and the trap that had caught this archive over martha maud was checked for: the district was searched with no mother's name at all, shenton at hitchin across twenty-one years, and there is exactly one shenton birth in it. william shenton married a wear at hitchin in q3 1918 and died there in q3 1953. louise s a shenton died at hitchin in q4 1967, aged 84 — and the initials close it, because her birth is registered as louisa sarah a wear, q1 1883, at kingston, surrey, which is a place neither of her parents had ever been put before. and emma hull died in q2 1944 at hitchin, aged eighty-five, four years after the grandson she had known as a boy was taken prisoner. eighty-five years from aldenham to letchworth, two husbands buried, and thirty miles.
wrote a grandmother over her own mother, by matching on a name withdrawn

did the pix road finding was applied to the tree by a script that selected people by name. emma hawkins the daughter, born 7 february 1859, and emma hawkins the mother, born about 1822, are two entries two generations apart with identical names — and the code did not look at the generation. for part of 17 september this archive published that a woman born about 1822 was blind at letchworth in 1939. the same run appended a sentence to the giddins household at norton end saying that their daughter emma was born on 7 february 1859; their emma is emma giddins, born about 1855 at norton, a different woman in a different parish who shares only a forename. both are withdrawn on the pages themselves. a match on a name is not a match on a person — which is the thing this archive says about every census index it touches, said while doing it.
caroline james stops being an index line and becomes a household documented

did the remarriage had rested on a gro index entry. the 1921 census settles it from both directions. there is no caroline castle anywhere in hertfordshire in 1921 — she leaves the surname exactly when the index says she changed it. and there is one caroline james: rg15/7079, schedule 125, 9 boscombe place, letchworth, wife of james james, born at weston, hertfordshire — with ernest albert cyril castle and florence margarite hilda castle in the house, enumerated as his step-children. that is an enumerator writing down a remarriage. her age, 56 years 4 months, puts her birthday in february and agrees with the 28th; the year is two out and she is the one who gave it. she had also moved to letchworth, where her daughter was raising the wears.
nine children born, eight living, and only six have been found documented

did the 1911 census at st mary's cottages, baldock — rg14/7572, schedule 173 — asks a married woman how many children she has borne. caroline answers nine born, eight living, one died. this archive has names for six from the gro index and a seventh in martha maud. so at least two castle children have never been identified and one of the nine was already dead by 1911. her own father, joseph wallis, is in the house as well, spelt wallis — a seventh independent instance of the spelling that was in dispute a day ago.
excluded the wrong frederick, with an exact date this time inferred

did frederick james castle, born 1889 at hitchin to a mother née wallis, is the only castle male line that could ever carry a y test. the frederick james castle who died at hitchin in 1975 is not him: the 1939 register has that man at 17 orchard road, baldock, born 10 april 1887, a vertical driller on aircraft work, married to ella. and baldock supplies the warning as well as the problem — a search of the 1921 census returns a second unrelated castle household at 5 cemetery road with nine children and its own frederick, born about april 1888. three men of one name in one small town within two years. our frederick is in no english census after 1901 and in no death index at all, which is now the open question rather than a solved one.
sixty-three and seventy-two pix road documented

did the 1939 register was searched for leonard's aunt louisa shenton and returned his grandmother. schedule 305, 63 pix road, letchworth: emma hull, born 7 february 1859, widowed, "incapacitated - blind"; louisa shenton, born 29 november 1882; william shenton, incapacitated. emma hull is emma hawkins — born at aldenham, widowed at thirty-one in 1890, remarried to john hull and widowed again. henry robert and martha maud had raised their six at 72 pix road, the same street. the register was taken on 29 september 1939, seven weeks after the last ship sailed, and it finds an eighty-year-old blind woman and the daughter keeping her still in the road the family had left. the record says who was where and nothing about what anybody felt. but it is no longer true that the family simply left.
learned that the paywall was not one documented

did the estate references looked to be behind a subscription. they are not: every south african estate over the threshold must be advertised as a form j193 notice in the government gazette, which is free and full-text to 2026. the only trick is the name order — modern notices read surname first. four estates in twenty minutes, all four women born wear, with exact birth dates, identity numbers and addresses.
oskar left theresienstadt on a card that names the transport at both ends documented

did his four arolsen person records were on the work list as “all openable and none read”. read, three of them lock together. the gestapo list of the “4th large transport of the elderly”, 17 march 1943, page 161 line 54: leibholz, oskar israel, 13.5.87, schubin, w.50 marburgerstr. 13, number 014577. an ajdc index card repeats it as “49/30999 ii — 4.gr.alterstrsp. 17.3.43” and adds his birthplace in full, schubin/bromberg, and his wife, gertrud geb. leibke, 13.7.94 berlin. and in terezín a czech clerk wrote out a card of the central transport file: deportace na východ, číslo er 606, dne 16.x.1944, with the original transport number 11025-i/90 — which is the berlin transport’s own designation. the two ends of the journey name each other. the card does not say where he was sent; it says east.
withdrawn: the document that was not a deportation form withdrawn

did on 17 september this archive found jacob, auguste and kurt sharing one arolsen docid in a series called deportations and transports, reasoned that it was “a deportation form that records a man’s household and his next of kin”, and called that reading “evidence instead of the charitable guess”. david ticked the consent and the document was opened. it is a berlin residents’ registration card, and the docid covers two separate images — the family’s card and a sheet of other households. kurt’s name is on the second sheet, not on his family’s card. the series name was read as the document. what the card does give is worth the correction: auguste’s birthplace in her own household’s hand — sauerbaum, the east prussian village her mother johanna thimm came from, which until today rested on a single census card.
tested a restriction instead of assuming it documented

did t/d 755.334 for heinz leibholz was listed as “may be restricted like oskar’s — but that has not been tested”. tested: eleven documents, creation date 1959–1988, and the page serves no docid, no image and no document list. the consent declaration does not reach the t/d repository at all. the same sweep listed every leibholz topic in the archive — forty-three of them — and the list is itself a finding: ten consecutive case numbers, 90.465 to 90.474, are one enquiry about one household, and they match the levetzowstraße 13 family from the 1939 census to the day. one of those ten is “leibholz, kurt”, and it is alfred’s son born in 1927, not derrick’s father. written down so nobody finds it later and draws the obvious wrong conclusion.
an emigration card with the word emigrating crossed out documented

did row 197 was written to ask whether oskar’s wife was on the transport that took him to theresienstadt, because she is not on the page that carries him. it was answered the same afternoon and the answer is no. the kultusvereinigung berlin — the community organisation the state had turned into an instrument of its own administration — kept zählkarten, counting cards, and hers survives: “leibholz geb. leibke · gertrud · 13.7.94, berlin · verh.”, household address marburgerstr. 13, written on 8 march 1943. the card is headed “zählkarte für auswandernde personen” with auswandernde struck through in ink, and in the column headed zielland — country of destination — somebody has written verstorben 27/2.43. she died eighteen days before the transport left. oskar’s line on the list carries no ehepaar bracket because by then there was no pair. the date itself was already published here from the memorial book, which is a compilation; it is now on a card filled in nine days later by the office that knew her.
two leibholz families, and they are finally separable by place documented

did the 43 tracing topics threw up “t/d 161.094 for meyer, gertrud born 09.03.1899”, indexed under the maiden name leibholz. a leibholz daughter born in 1899 would have fitted the schubin family, which has no sister in it at all, and a row was written to chase her. her second person record answers it in one word: place of birth glowitz — główczyce, kreis stolp, in pomerania. that is willi’s district, not jacob’s. she is a pomeranian leibholz and she is not anybody’s sister here. the negative is worth more than the hypothesis was: for weeks the two leibholz families could only be told apart by argument, and now they can be told apart by place — schubin in posen against stolp in pommern, with two documented birthplaces on each side. her own fate is on the record: wave 48, the 34th osttransport to auschwitz, 4 march 1943 — thirteen days before oskar went to theresienstadt, on a different kind of list altogether.
searched the names database by who wrote the page, and found somebody alive documented

did a page of testimony names the person who filled it in, and so does a relico questionnaire, so searching the submitter field asks a different question: not who died but who survived to write it down. submitter last name leibholz returns three records and one woman — sophie leibholz, filling in forms for the world jewish congress relief committee in shanghai in 1946. she was looking for her brother sally binder, a tailor of motzstrasse 13 in neukölln, deported to auschwitz on 1 march 1943; for his wife mathilde; and for her brother-in-law heinrich leibholz, born berlin 16 october 1890, a tax agent of hornstrasse 19, wife agnes. heinrich is this archive’s control case — the man used to prove that vanishing from the berlin directory after 1942 does not mean death, because he died in 1948. he now has a birth date, a wife, a street and a trade, and somebody was looking for him from shanghai two years before he died, not knowing he had lived. nothing ties any of them to kurt’s family, and it is the first leibholz survivor this archive has a name for.
withdrawn: the niece who was a niece by marriage withdrawn

did the work list has argued for three days that irmgard shtern was the best lead in the archive on the oldest open question — whether georg leibholz’s line touches sally leibholz and friederike schmul of schubin. the argument was clean: she called herself georg’s niece, so her parent was georg’s sibling, so her other pages of testimony would name georg’s parents. she filed seventeen of them, and three of them end it. lidia laibholz b.1884 gives her father as elius and her mother as mina; klara lewinzon b.1906 gives yulius and mina; ema mendelzon b.1892 gives yulius and meine. elius and yulius are one name through the hebrew and so are mina and meine. they are three sisters, and irmgard is niece to all three — so georg is the uncle by marriage, her blood is lydia’s family, and her pages could never have given georg’s parents. georg’s own page has no father and no mother on it and gives his birthplace as the single word germany. what the seventeen did give: lydia’s parents and two sisters, which nobody had — and gideon shtruzik, born 1940, marital status “child”, of berlin, murdered, father harry. harry struzik was elli leibholz’s husband, so gideon is almost certainly elli’s son and georg’s grandson, although his mother is not named on the page.
followed a survivor to shanghai and found her husband’s death certificate in a list documented

did this morning’s find was a name and a city: sophie leibholz, filling in relief questionnaires in shanghai in 1946, the first leibholz survivor this archive had a name for. who she was married to was unknown. mapping the lives has an emigration place field nobody here had used — surname leibholz, emigration place shanghai, two results, and one of them is albert leibholz born 17 may 1886, who is the “albert, antiquitäten, halensee” of the 1938 berlin directory. arolsen then has him twice. a central location index card, l 337909: “leibholz · albert · died 8.18.44 · 5.17.86 · berlin · dealer · last known address shanghai” — and under other members of the family abroad, “sophie · w · 6.19.87 · berlin”. w is wife. the card also carries the crossing — “arr. 6.27.39 from berlin” — and a third person looking for them, curt sterngast of rehavia, jerusalem. and the h.i.a.s. list of jewish nationals who died and were buried in shanghai 1939–1948, page 24: “leibholz, albert · 5/17/86 · 8/18/44 · paralisis progressitis”. a berlin antiques dealer, out on 27 june 1939 with ten weeks to spare, dead in shanghai in 1944, his widow still there in december 1945. it also separates the two sophie leibholzes for good — née binder, born berlin 19 june 1887, alive; née rothenberg, born schlochau 9 january 1887, murdered. none of it touches kurt’s family, and it is the first leibholz household this archive has followed all the way out.
searched the census by address instead of by name, and found our own kreis in charlottenburg documented

did every earlier pass at the 1939 census database started from a surname in the berlin directory. starting from a street and house number returns the whole flat, and it produced a correction and a household. the correction is this archive’s own: levetzowstraße 13 holds six leibholz, not five — walter, born 20.09.1922, was simply missed, and he is the t/d case 90.473 that looked like a name the census lacked. the household is danckelmannstraße 44, charlottenburg, which this archive has listed for a week as a leibholz stolperstein “belonging to another family”. hans leibholz, born 25 january 1912 at preussisch friedland, kreis schlochau, deported from berlin on 12 january 1943 and dead at auschwitz on 22 february; his mother else née rothenberg, born at schlochau; his sister liselott, born at preussisch friedland; and a second rothenberg woman of 1884, laura, in the same flat. kreis schlochau is hammerstein’s district, and hammerstein is where sally leibholz — jacob’s father, derrick’s great-grandfather — was born on 7 july 1847. every other berlin household placed so far is schubin, stolp or berlin; this is the first from our own kreis. a district is not a family and this archive has been burnt twice by good fits, so it is not claimed as kinship. what it does is name the place to write to, and nobody here has ever asked poland for a hammerstein record.
proposed writing to poland for a letter that was answered six days ago withdrawn

did the charlottenburg household led to kreis schlochau, and kreis schlochau is where sally leibholz was born, so a row was written saying nobody here had ever asked poland for a hammerstein record and it was time to. somebody had. a letter went to archiwum państwowe w koszalinie on 14 september asking for exactly those two records — sally’s birth of 1847 and georg’s of 1884 — and the synagogue books. it was answered on 16 september, reference o-s.6342.406.2026, signed by the head of the słupsk branch: no standesamt hammerstein registers for 1874 to 1899, no synagogue-community books for czarne at all, and no information about where either went. it was acknowledged on the 17th. what the morning’s work adds is one line of corroboration: the public finding aid holds fond 27/364/0, standesamt hammerstein [czarne], at koszalin’s słupsk branch, 127 digitised units, and its own date facet reads 1900+ : 128, 1800–1899 : 0. the branch’s written negative is confirmed by its own catalogue. that is worth a line and it is not worth a row. six times in one day now, and the cause has not changed: a row or a paragraph written off the back of a fresh find without first reading the file that already answers it. the rule that follows is one command — grep letters.json and requests/ for the place name before proposing to write to anybody.
the surname that cannot be searched in a newspaper inferred

did priority three of the findmypast subscription is a newspaper sweep of the hitchin and letchworth titles for wear and castle notices. it was tried, and the instrument will not do it. wear is one of the commonest words in british newspaper advertising, and unlike the census sets the newspaper name box is an ocr string match rather than an index of transcribed names. wear with the keyword letchworth returns 9,442 articles headed “men’s wear at pugh’s, letchworth”; “martha maud wear” returns 285 headed by a knitting joke and a yorkshire sock advertisement. two further properties of the tool go down beside the rule that its marriage index silently returns zero when year-filtered: the exact-keyword switch does not enforce a phrase, so “pix road” with it ticked returns 85,719 articles — and the results url ignores the county and date parameters, so this one set cannot be swept by constructing urls the way every other set can. a query with all five filters returned twenty million, more than the unfiltered one. the sweep is re-scoped rather than abandoned: it has to be driven by strings that are not ordinary english — shenton, giddins, wallis with baldock — and by the ship names, windsor castle in march 1937 and dunvegan castle in august 1939, looking for a departure notice. the surname on its own is not worth trying again.
the broken year filter is not only the marriages withdrawn

did on 16 september this archive proved that findmypast’s marriage index silently returns zero when year-filtered, using a positive control — james shardalow mort, married at yarmouth in 1885, who disappears when the search is narrowed to 1885 give or take two. the rule written then named the marriage index. looking for the six hitchin wear children in hertfordshire baptisms found the same defect in a second set. lastname smith, no year: 15,122 baptisms. the same search narrowed to 1880 give or take five: zero. fifteen thousand hertfordshire smiths and not one of them baptised between 1875 and 1885. the 1920 window also returns zero, and without the 1880 control that would have been read as “the set does not reach the twentieth century” and written down as a coverage bound. the rule is restated wider: never year-filter a findmypast search in any set, and if one is run, run a positive control in the same set in the same breath. the failure mode is the dangerous one — a clean, plausible zero instead of an error. the children themselves are not there: eleven wear baptisms in the whole county set, the latest 1891, the only hitchin one 1786 — and a whole-category search for cynthia y e wear, born hitchin 1931, returns her gro birth entry and no parish baptism anywhere.
a user tree’s date, confirmed to the day by a government index documented

did priority seven of the findmypast subscription is probate, and it paid. george william castle the younger — martha maud’s elder brother — has been carried here on a date taken from a match holder’s tree and nothing else: died 23 august 1939. the england & wales government probate death index has him: death date 23 aug 1939, residence town letchworth, probate granted at the london registry on 2 november 1939, linked person cyril george castle. two things come with it. he was in letchworth — the wears’ town, and the youngest castle brother was at 9 boscombe place, letchworth in the 1921 census; the castles had moved from baldock and the wears went to the same place. and the dates sit thirteen days apart: martha maud sailed from london on the dunvegan castle on 10 august 1939, and her brother died at letchworth on the 23rd. she had been gone a fortnight. both halves are documented — bt27 on one side, the probate index on the other. cyril george castle is a new name and is not the ninth child, ernest albert cyril castle of baldock; likeliest a son of the deceased, and not asserted. the original calendar page would give the street, the occupation, the executors and the estate value, and it could not be read: findmypast’s image gateway is session-locked and returns 403 to anything outside the signed-in browser.
line 1039, and he was not taken from the family flat documented

did this archive has had jacob leibholz’s deportation date since the gedenkbuch was checked on day two. what it never had was the paperwork, and the paperwork moves him to a different street. wave 44, the 30th osttransport to auschwitz of 26 february 1943, page 153, line 1039: “leibholz · jakob israel · 8.8.84 · schubin · beruf ohne · verh. ja · alter 58 · arbeitsfähig ja · wohnung treuchtlingerstr. 4 · kennkarte a492552 · kennzeichen 31822.” an ajdc index card repeats the address and adds one word: b/spier — bei spier, care of a family called spier. the same page of the list carries “49 b/grindel”, “b/gottfeld” and “b/neumann” against other names, so the convention is not a guess: he was lodging in somebody else’s flat, as many of the 1,100 were. the 1939 census has him at meraner strasse 2 with auguste and siegfried. between may 1939 and february 1943 he was moved out of his own home, and nothing read here says when or by whom; the word judenhaus is on neither document and is not used. one column is worth reading twice. in the 1938 directory he is jaques, kaufmann, with a clothing firm at krausenstraße 59–60. on the list of february 1943 the occupation column says ohne. and samuel, re-searched with the consent now ticked, is still not in the arolsen index at all — the second test of an absence this archive first recorded on 17 september.
two letters on a card, and a house already full documented

did the ajdc card for jacob leibholz ends “treuchtlingerstr. 4 b/spier”. searching the 1939 census by street and house number instead of by surname turns the two letters into three people: spier, max, born 12 april 1864, died 26 march 1941; spier, hans, born 2 december 1894; spier, alice née wollstein, born 3 november 1899, the last two both dead before 8 may 1945. and it says what kind of building it was. treuchtlinger straße 4 held seventeen persecuted people from eleven family names on census night — brück, cohn, eisenberg, eisenberger, kaphan, kochanowska, löwenheim, podbielski, rosenstock, sundheimer, spier. jacob was moved into a house that was already full, three and a half years before the transport. the same search on meraner strasse 2 solved something else. fourteen people at the family’s own address, and one of them is anna puff, born 1 june 1895 — who is one of the eleven names indexed on docid 11214358, the registration card whose second image nobody here could account for. so that second image is the house list for meraner strasse 2, which is exactly what the stamp on the first image says: “lt. hausliste 1945 n. erfaßt”. one exact match out of seven unplaced names, and the other six would not be in a database of persecuted people if they were not jewish — a strong reading, not a proof. it also gives kurt’s name on that sheet a reason at last: an absent son written against his parents’ flat. that is the third account this archive has given of why he is on that docid. it is offered as the best one and it is flagged as the third.
samuel had a wife, and the census had her all along documented

did the address search was then run across every leibholz address the berlin directory had given, and the best of them is kommandantenstraße 29 — samuel the hat wholesaler’s. it returns two people on consecutive census cards: samuel leibholz, born 28.06.1877 in szubin, “race” jjjj, deported to auschwitz, died 10 april 1943, card vz153419 — and frida leibbholz née spree, born 12 may 1888 in berlin, “race” nnnn, no date of death, card vz153420. so both brothers were in mixed marriages. jacob married auguste née luwinski, nnnn, persecuted “collectively”; samuel married frida née spree, nnnn. two men from schubin, two non-jewish german wives, and both men deported anyway. neither wife has a death date. a mischehe delayed the two brothers and it did not save them. samuel is not in the arolsen index at all, searched twice, the second time with the consent ticked — so the gap there is arolsen’s. the clerk spelt her surname leibbholz, with a doubled b. the same sweep separated the two wilhelms at last: the weinstraße 6 vertreter is born 30.12.1887 and yad vashem’s deported wilhelm 28.12.1890, so they are not one man. and it produced a coincidence that was checked and did not survive. at weinstraße 6, in the same building as a leibholz household, lives henriette rosenfeld née schmul — and schmul is friederike’s surname, jacob’s mother, married to sally leibholz at szubin in 1874. her record was opened inside a minute: born at swinemünde in pomerania, not schubin, not posen. the coincidence is real and the connection is not evidenced, and it is written down so the next reader does not spend an hour on it.
opened the half of the address books nobody here had opened documented

did every earlier pass at the berliner adressbücher read teil i, householders by name. there is a teil iv that lists the same people by street, house by house, with the owner first and the tenants beneath — and it answers the one question teil i cannot: who else lived in the building. the 1939 volume, printed page 1629, gives treuchtlinger straße 4 entire: “4 e eisenberg, g., vw. handelsgerichtsrat · bayer, oberstleutnant · eberhardt, kaufmann · jakob, maurer · mannowsky · petras · rosenstock · spier, h., handelsvertreter · — m., vertreter · sundheimer · wendorf”. the e is eigentümer: the house belonged to gertrud eisenberg née haake, born 9 june 1879, a commercial court councillor’s widow, who also lived in it. spier h. is hans, born 2 december 1894; the dash line under him is max, born 12 april 1864, dead by march 1941 — the same dash convention that cost this archive four leibholz households in a day last week. and the instrument is the bigger find. digital.zlb.de runs a goobi viewer with a solr query api: a post to /viewer/api/v1/index/query/ returns the image number of every page in a volume containing a word, and /pages/{n}/text/ returns that page’s ocr. three limits were measured and written down. fraktur ocr mangles words — “treuchtlinger” returns nothing in teil iv and the fuzzy form “treuchtlinger~1” returns exactly the two right pages. the teil iv ocr is column-interleaved and reads as nonsense, so it finds a page and cannot read one. and the table of contents gives printed page numbers, not image numbers: printed 1629 is image 5933, an offset of about 4,304 that differs per volume. the whole lookup took six requests.
went looking for corroboration, got one match and six misses, and kept the reading anyway inferred

did teil iv was then turned on the family’s own address. meraner straße 2, 1939, printed page 1598: the owner is salomonski, m., living away at tauentzienstraße in w 50, and the householders under him are binder, briliant, dübe, dunje, gadischle & kaulmann, hesler, helm, kamnitzer, v. koch, leibholz, j., kfm. , neumann, pehser, putzar-ehrenberg, schade twice, wesse. jacob is listed at his own address as a kaufmann — the trade the transport list of 1943 would record as ohne. and it was a test, not a victory lap. this morning this archive decided that the unexplained second image of docid 11214358 is the house list for meraner straße 2, on the strength of anna puff appearing both on it and in the 1939 census at that address, plus the stamp “lt. hausliste 1945”. the directory was checked against the sheet’s other six names — schmidt, heinicke, herzog, biere, koch, nicksch — and not one of them is a householder there in 1939. the reading survives for two ordinary reasons and they are written down as an argument rather than a fact: the directory lists householders only, so lodgers never appear in it — anna puff herself does not — and a list stamped 1945 in a city where the bombed-out were rehoused constantly should not match a 1939 householder list. it is now a reading with a test behind it instead of a reading with one match behind it.
three luwinskis in post-war berlin, with trades, addresses and a telephone number documented

did the solr api found this morning searches forty volumes in one request, so the post-war berlin books were swept by surname for the first time — 27 namenteil volumes 1949–1970 and 13 telephone books 1969–1980, all set in antiqua, so the text layer reads cleanly and no page images are needed. luwinski returns ten pages in eight volumes and three men, every one already in the family tree and every one dead. manfred, “schlosser” and then modellschlosser, tegel, egellsstraße 16, from 1957 to 1970 — and modellschlosser is model fitter, the exact trade on the 1965 icem emigration roll that flew him to melbourne care of a mr h. marquardt, and the tree holds helga erna marquardt née luwinski. three sources, one man. joachim, ofensetzer — a stove-fitter — of ramlerstraße 15, wedding, in 1967 and 1970: a trade and an address the tree does not have for him at all. and kurt, a post-office worker at stephanstraße 7 in 1964 and peter-vischer-straße 25 in 1967, who by the 1970–71 telephone book is “luwinski kurt · 4 12 25 12 · beamter · 52 waldstr. 60”. that kurt is not derrick’s father, who left germany in 1933 and died in johannesburg in 1968 and cannot be in a 1970 berlin telephone book. it is the tree’s other kurt, leo’s son, recorded as dying in 1995 with no birth date, no place and no occupation. a surname, a city and an era: a correspondence, not an identification, and written down as one. oskar luwinski, the master tailor of steglitzer straße in 1933, is in none of the forty volumes.
a candidate in one year, and in no other inferred

did the same sweep did the other half of row 179. “fricke auguste” across all forty post-war volumes returns three pages and they are two women. the 1957 namenteil has “fricke auguste rentn chlb 1 kais-friedr-str 79”, a pensioner in charlottenburg — the candidate for kurt’s mother under her last married name. the 1963 and 1970 street sections have “fricke auguste putzfrau” in the same building both years, among fröhlich, kaldenbach, luckow and stinka. a working cleaner in 1963 is not the seventy-year-old pensioner of 1957. and the pensioner appears in no other volume of the run, and in no telephone book. four fricke blocks were opened by hand as well — 1952, 1954, 1963, 1970 — and none holds an auguste under her own name or on the dash. if she is lizzy, she was in berlin in 1957 and gone by 1959 — and she was still in berlin two years after her mother died at zeutern in october 1955. she did not go to baden to nurse her mother. she went afterwards, and died at kraichtal, the same town, in 1975. the identification is still unproved and nothing here changes that: one line, no age, no birth date, no maiden name. what the sweep buys is the difference between “there is a candidate in 1957” and “there is a candidate in 1957 and in no other year”.
asked the opposite question of the berlin directories, and heinrich’s widow answered it documented

did every pass at these books has tracked the surname disappearing — seventeen leibholz householders in 1938, six in 1942, every name carrying israel gone. nobody here had asked who was still there afterwards. the post-war run is forty volumes to 1980 and set in antiqua, so it searches outright. leibholz returns nineteen pages in seventeen volumes and six names across thirty years. agnes is the one that closes a loop. “leibholz agnes, rentn., sw 61 mehringdamm 109” in 1957 and 1959, and still at mehringdamm 109 in the 1975–76 telephone book — nineteen years at one address, with a line of her own by the end. heinrich leibholz is this archive’s control case, the man who proved that vanishing from the directory after 1942 does not mean death, because he died on 9 august 1948; the census gives his wife as agnes née kerger, born 1889. and sophie leibholz, filling in a relief questionnaire in shanghai in 1946, named him with “wife agnes” and asked where he was. he had survived; he died two years later; his widow lived on at mehringdamm for another quarter-century. the others are ella the nurse at dominicusstraße and then willmanndamm, charlotte at hasenheide, gerhard a doctor of economics in steglitz — not the constitutional lawyer of the same name, who died at göttingen — felix at wiesbadener straße 57 and then hilde in the same flat, and erna alone in spandau in 1980. not one is documented as belonging to the schubin family, and that is the point: the survivors of this surname in berlin are the other leibholz families. kurt’s people were in johannesburg, in potsdam, and in a grave at auschwitz. one absence was looked for on purpose — frida leibbholz née spree, samuel’s non-jewish widow with no death date, is in none of the forty volumes. telephone numbers were deliberately not transcribed.
the geneteka zero was a one-character bug, and the control had been right all along withdrawn

did on 20 september this archive searched geneteka, the polish genealogical society’s index, for leibholz marriages in kujawsko-pomorskie and got nothing — then ran kowalski as a control, got nothing again, and correctly refused to publish the negative. the cause is now found and it is one character. geneteka’s province codes are positional: 01ds dolnośląskie, 02kp kujawsko-pomorskie, 03lb lubelskie, 04ls lubuskie. the query used w=04kp, which does not exist, so the select fell back silently to dolnośląskie and every search ran against the wrong province. there is a second trap in the same site: the results table is filled by ajax after the page loads, so a plain fetch of the search url returns the shell with an empty table, which reads exactly like a zero. with w=02kp the control passes — kowalski returns thousands from 1621 on. and the real answers arrive. leibholz: zero in kujawsko-pomorskie and zero in wielkopolskie, births and marriages alike. schmul: eighteen marriages in wielkopolskie, fuzzy across szmul, szmił, schmul, szmiel and szmielewski — lwówek, przedecz, pyzdry, turek, dąbie, krotoszyn, gniezno, pniewy, koło — and not one at szubin. and there is a structural reason none could be. szubin is in geneteka — parish 13066, indexed from 1715 — but it is the catholic parish. geneteka marks jewish registers “(mojż.)”, and kujawsko-pomorskie contains no (mojż.) parish at all, not one across 358 entries. so geneteka cannot answer the szubin question and never could. sally leibholz’s marriage to friederike schmul on 24 november 1874 needs the letter to bydgoszcz, which is drafted and unsent — and that is now a tested statement instead of an assumption.
the register this archive has been writing letters about is online documented

did geneteka having been proved structurally incapable of holding a jewish szubin record, the question became where the 1874 register actually is. it is in three places and one of them needs no letter at all. archiwum państwowe w bydgoszczy holds the szubin civil registers in three fonds — 6/1792/0 szubin miasto, 1874–1935, with marriages from 1874 and, crucially, skorowidze, alphabetical indexes, for 1874–1878; 6/1795/0 wieś i; 6/1796/0 wieś ii. and familysearch filmed them from bydgoszcz. catalogue koha:402152, standesamt i, film note “geburten, heiraten, tote 1874–1876”, digital film 007998644, 1,121 images. catalogue koha:402191, standesamt ii, 1874–1875, digital film 008016003, 1,160 images. both open in the viewer with no restriction and no affiliate-library wall. neither is in the full-text index — the service’s own groupnumber lookup returns an empty id list for both — so they cannot be searched by surname and have to be browsed. that is tractable rather than hopeless: prussian civil registration began on 1 october 1874, so the 1874 volumes cover three months, the marriage book should hold a few dozen entries, and the skorowidz should be a single page. a marriage register of 1874 names the parents of both spouses. that is the generation above sally leibholz and friederike schmul, and nobody in this family has ever had it. request 30 to bydgoszcz has been updated to cite the three fond references, so a busy office does not have to find them — and if the browse succeeds the letter is only needed for a certified copy, if at all.
withdrawn: an image count is not an image withdrawn

did an hour ago this archive published that the szubin civil registers of 1874 are filmed and that “both are online and neither is restricted — no permission wall, no affiliate-library restriction, no login beyond the ordinary free account”. that is wrong and it is withdrawn. the claim was made from the viewer reporting a page count — 1,121 images for film 007998644, 1,160 for 008016003 — without looking at the page, because the browser pane was hidden and only the text layer was being read. with the pane displayed, every thumbnail in the filmstrip carries a padlock, and opening one returns familysearch’s own notice: “image restricted. image access is typically determined by local laws or the custodian who has the original document. to view these images do one of the following: access the site at a familysearch center.” the lesson is general and goes beside the others. familysearch serves a film’s length to everybody, restricted or not. the padlocks exist only in the rendered page. a film’s availability cannot be read from its metadata, and reading a count as an answer is the same mistake as reading a dead hostname as a dead service. what survives is most of it: the registers exist, they are at archiwum państwowe w bydgoszczy in three named fonds, the town fond has skorowidze — alphabetical indexes — for 1874–1878, and the films are 007998644 and 008016003. only the viewing is blocked, and by the custodian rather than by familysearch. and it leaves a free route this archive cannot take itself. the restriction lifts inside a familysearch centre or affiliate library, of which there are several in brisbane, and access there costs nothing. film 007998644, the 1874 skorowidz, the marriage of sally leibholz and friederike schmul on 24 november 1874 — an afternoon at a terminal. request 30 to bydgoszcz is therefore necessary after all, and it is a better letter for citing the three fond references.
checked the polish side too, and the register is unreachable from any desk inferred

did having got the familysearch answer wrong once, the rest was checked properly. film 008016003, standesamt ii, is padlocked as well — so the restriction is on the szubin material, not on one reel. and the polish state archives’ own portal has no scans of it either: szukajwarchiwach returns the three usc szubin fonds at fond level only, with no unit rows, no inventory and no scan counts, across four differently-worded searches. the control is what makes that a finding rather than a shrug. the same search box returns 127 unit-level rows, each with a “number of scans” line, for “standesamt hammerstein” at koszalin’s słupsk branch. the portal does show units and does show scans when they exist. it has neither for szubin. so the position is now fully mapped: the registers exist and nobody can see them from a desk. not digitised in poland; filmed by the mormons and locked to a familysearch centre. two routes remain and both need a person in a room — a free terminal at a familysearch centre in brisbane, or the letter to bydgoszcz, drafted and unsent.
the town’s paper stops twenty years before the family left inferred

did the newspaper sweep was re-run the way the re-scoping said — drive the filter panel, and search strings that are not ordinary english. first, why the panel works now: the browser pane had been hidden, and a click cannot reach a pane that is not compositing frames, so every earlier attempt to open a facet failed with the panel apparently inert. displaying it fixed the problem instantly — and the same hidden pane is what produced the szubin padlock error an hour later. twice in one day, one cause. the ship was the best idea and it came back empty. keyword “dunvegan castle”, 47,783 articles, faceted to hertfordshire: eleven. 1890, 1897 twice, 1898, 1900, 1901 twice, 1902 — then 1982 twice and 1986. mrs louis botha landing at southampton, and coach tours to skye. not one in 1939. and then the coverage was checked, which should have come first. letchworth has exactly one digitised title: citizen (letchworth), 1906–1917, 587 issues. the wears lived at 72 pix road and left in 1937–39. the town’s only digitised paper stops twenty years before they went. hitchin has exactly one, the hertfordshire express, 1859~1956 — and 1,403 issues across ninety-seven years is fourteen a year for a weekly, a quarter-sampled run at best. so the priority closes rather than being re-scoped again. a departure notice for this family is not findable here, and the reason is neither the search nor the surname: the paper was never digitised for the years that mattered. that is a coverage bound and it is the end of the route.
sauerbaum is zerbuń, and one spelling is not a search documented

did two of the twenty were done at once, and the second was rescued by david. first: sauerbaum, kreis rössel, is zerbuń — today in gmina jeziorany, powiat olsztyński. its parish and civil district were bössau: groß bössau is biesowo, and the amtsbezirk bössau was formed on 9 july 1874 with its seat there, so the standesamt bössau is where auguste’s birth of 28 august 1893 must be registered. every polish archive and portal is organised on the current name, and this archive has spent weeks searching a german one. second: geneteka’s east prussian province, never searched until today. the first pass ran one spelling, found one woman in one village, and wrote “nothing else in the entire province”. david then said to try every spelling. the instruction changed the result. lowinski returns three births at standesamt rössel — franz 1876, albert 1881, bernhard 1884 — and kreis rössel is the district sauerbaum is in, where johanna thimm was born in 1871 and auguste in 1893. luwenski returns the best lead of the day: entry eleven of the new allenstein civil registry, 1874 — martha luwenski, father joseph, mother elisabeth bilitewski. joachim luwinski was born at allenstein in 1865, and the family tree already holds a joseph luwinski with no dates, inside the hundred-name polish block this archive has always called a surname index rather than a descent. it is the first time that block has touched a record. the same registry spells one woman lowinski in four years and luwinski in two, which is the whole argument in one line. neither find is claimed as kinship. both name exactly which entries olsztyń should be asked for. and the rule goes down: one spelling is not a search. every surname sweep from here runs the archive’s whole documented list of variants, one at a time, exact.

ten files a year, scanned free, and a status this archive will not claim inferred

did the landesarchiv's own page says relatives of nazi-persecuted people, or those they authorise, may have up to ten files a year digitised at no charge, and that the quota covers wiedergutmachungs- and haftakten too. the letter mentions it and does not assert it. derrick is kurt's son on every document there is, and this archive has published at length the dna result that puts that paternity in doubt. the german text says so plainly and leaves the decision to them. an archive that has questioned a relationship in public does not quietly rely on it in private.

did tried again an hour after the first failure. the application loaded; the search box was clicked, the surname typed a character at a time, return pressed, and the submit button clicked twice — once by coordinate, once by element reference. the results area never populated and no search request was ever sent: the network log holds the configuration calls and the fonts and nothing else, and the console is clean. trove has not been searched. not one query has run, and anything said here about what it holds would be invention. the ryerson index answered “server overloaded” to six attempts in the same sitting.
asked olsztyn for a marriage, not a birth documented

did the letter to the warmia archive is drafted, and it asks first for the marriage of joachim luwinski and johanna thimm — undated, but bracketed between her birth in 1871 and their daughter's in 1893, so somewhere about 1888 to 1893 at biesowo or reszel. a marriage record names the parents of both parties. johanna's are known; joachim's are known to nobody, and they are the oldest generation reachable on this side. it also names the four indexed entries the spelling sweep found — allenstein 1874 no. 11, reszel 1876 no. 68, 1881 no. 31, 1884 no. 9 — so an archivist can go straight to the book. and it gets the 1874 line right: civil registration began on 1 october that year, so the 1865 and 1871 births are church records, and the letter asks whether those books sit at olsztyn or at the archdiocesan archive.

did a running head names the first and last street on a page, not the street a column belongs to — and taking a number from one entry and a name from its neighbour is exactly the error that produced the false estate notice in september. so the heading was hunted down on the previous page: “no. 55 · chodowieckistr. · a.g. berl. mitte — l.g. i”, with the numbers running unbroken from 1 to 40 before the street ends at an arrow marked greifswalder str. and a new heading begins. the corner confirms it: 32 is marked “s. a. winsstr. 42” and 33 “s. a. winsstr. 33”, consecutive numbers facing each other across a junction. a text-layer hit is not a read entry: the ocr gave the name and swallowed the street, the number, the neighbour and the initial.
standesamt berlin viii, 1912, number 963 documented

did kurt's birth entry, found. “luwinski · kurt myszislaus. · 963”, the fourth line of the may block in the l section of p rep. 523 nr. 1395, the landesarchiv's name index to the birth register of standesamt berlin viii for 1912. twenty-one candidate volumes became one in three steps: schöneberg excluded by reading its entire 1912 l section; the 1913 directory giving chodowieckistraße 32; and the berliner adressbuch's own street index, whose first column is headed standesamt, giving houses 23 to 32 as office 8. four things then agree — surname, forename, month, and a district arrived at independently — and the arithmetic checks: entry 963 of a register that passes 2561 by december sits 37.6 per cent through it, and 11 may is 36 per cent through the year. every l page of 1912 was read; there is exactly one luwinski in the whole year.
a second forename nobody has ever seen documented

did myszislaus. not the family tree, not the arolsen index, not the berlin registration card, not one south african document has ever carried a second forename for kurt. it is a german clerk's spelling of the polish mieczysław — and it is the first thing this archive has learned about him that came from him rather than about him.
schöneberg ii, 1924, number six — and the clerk wrote down the mischehe documented

did the marriage entry, found. “leibholz · mos. · verheiratet mit luwinski · kath. · nr. 6”, and the same entry again under her name, on page 221 of the marriage index of standesamt schöneberg ii. the tree gives the wedding as 5 january 1924; a register restarts at 1 each january and the entries above are 1, 2 and 4, so the sixth marriage of the year is a marriage in the first week of it — date and number agreeing without either being derived from the other. and the registrar wrote the religions: mos. against jacob, kath. against auguste. her catholicism had been inferred from the ermland, from sauerbaum and from a census card. here it is written down at her own wedding, in the same line as her husband's judaism.

did two transcribers disagreed about sally leibholz's mother: this archive read wilhelmine at the image on 22 september, the portal's volunteer indexer read philipine. settled on 27 september without preferring either, by asking what this registrar's letters look like where the answer is already known. his capital p — four words along the same line, in pollnow — is a single round bowl, and the disputed capital has no bowl at all; philipine is out on the same stroke of the same nib. his capital h — in hammerstein, written twice on the page as the groom's birthplace and residence — has a long flat baseline lead-in, two steep diagonals and a low crossbar joining them, and the disputed capital has all three. so the name begins with h, the rest is x-height minims at the scan's limit, and she is published as “h—— geb. pollnow”. henriette is the name that would occur to anyone reading a jewish prussian register of 1874, which is exactly why it is not written down. stated weakness: kurrent w and h are alike and there is no w in this hand anywhere on the spread, so w is excluded on the positive h match rather than on a w exemplar. and the earlier reasoning is named: a pass this same week read philipine and defended it by claiming a w “has no ascender loop” — false, and worse, a claim about the alphabet in general with an exemplar sitting four words away.

did derrick's summary panel said his father was “kurt israel luwinski, of record — disputed by dna”. the exclusion had been published for a fortnight: 0.0% ashkenazi where a quarter would be required, a y haplogroup that is north sea rather than ashkenazi, and the tree page grading him ruled out and saying in as many words that this is not a level on the ladder but a claim tested and failed. the exclusion is not a dispute and it is not open. what is open is who the biological father was. a peer session then copied that phrase off the panel into a chart note, so the page contradicted itself within one screen — the panel saying disputed, the chart beneath it saying excluded and settled — and the peer found it when i corrected their note without correcting the sentence they had taken it from. it was true when written and was never read against the finding that replaced it. and it exposes a blind spot in the gate this archive built yesterday for exactly this fault. check-superseded refuses a build that still asserts a withdrawn value — a date, a name — because a value is declared and a string can be matched. this was not a stale value but a stale characterisation: nobody had thought to declare “disputed” as a withdrawn way of describing a settled exclusion, so there was nothing for the gate to match. declared now, as the third fact in data/superseded.json, which is the only fix available — the gate cannot find what nobody declares, and its coverage is exactly as wide as somebody’s memory. the peer reports the same shape twice more in the estate this week: an /about page saying the living were “absent from the build” while six were named in its own living.json, and a /register saying “not one is living” in an archive holding a living woman. three instances, one class: a true sentence left standing beside the data that replaced it.

did the count is the useful part. the rosebank scan was written up as new when every field on it had been on the dna page for five days, rebuilt from familysearch tiles. a row was raised saying the sandf request had been turned from a guess into a document, when it was drafted with that evidence already in it. a follow-up letter was drafted asking the parish for two books its own email had already ruled out — because only the pdf attachment had been opened and not the message. the pattern is consistent: the new artefact gets read and the context around it does not — the email body, the existing page, the rejection list. five of the six were caught by a control or by david rather than by the rule that exists to catch them.
a bound is not a date, and four of them were being printed as dates documented

did year() takes the first four digits of a date string and throws the qualifier away. so “before 1955” reached the bloodline as 1955 and the timeline plotted a point at it; “after may 13 1942” likewise. four people were affected. fixed in the builder rather than the data: every record now carries byq/dyq beside by/dy, the correction loop sets them so a correction cannot re-introduce the fault, and both pages print the word. one of the four was then replaced outright — elli leibholz's “after may 13 1942” is the deportation date, and gedenkbuch entry en1169257 has her dying at kulmhof in may 1942, birth date matching to the day.
the name search was the wrong instrument, and a healthy control hid it for a day withdrawn

did row 251 asked for one cheap thing: bracket friedrich leipholz’s disappearance from the berlin telephone books the way erna’s was. a full-text sweep of all twelve volumes answered it immediately — present in four, absent in eight — and the answer was false. reading the slot instead of searching the name turned eight zeros into six positives and two verified absences. the ocr prints this surname leiphotz in 1972-73, lelpholz in 1976-77 and 1978-79, leipkslz in 1977-78 and leibholz in 1980-81: five of the eleven readable volumes mangle it, and a search for the correct spelling misses every one. what licensed the error was a control that looked healthy — schmidt, 133 to 191 hits a volume, in every book that has a text layer at all. it cannot clear a rare-name negative: a volume can be richly indexed and still lose one line to a broken glyph. the fix is the instrument row 252 already uses on the death registers — leipholz sorts between leipert and leipic, so print the whole slot and read it, and treat a missing side as inconclusive rather than negative. it gained a third friedrich volume, made erna’s run continuous across all six, and moved the bracket a year: he is in 1973-74 and the slot is complete and empty in 1974-75. and the bracket then disagreed with the registers — reinickendorf 1974-1981 is already read in full and he is in none of it, so the tidy reading, that he left the book because he died, is the one thing this cannot say.
the firm was in the wrong street, and the proof was a letter that is not there withdrawn

did reading the adressbuch householder runs for row 260 — as runs, not as a name search — turned up two published facts that did not survive. the 1940 volume holds ten leibholz householders and three files said eleven, with the correct enumeration of ten printed directly beneath the claim in one of them; the eleven belongs to 1939. and jaques leibholz & co., jacob’s own firm, was at krausenstrasse 59-60 and this site had it at kronenstrasse on the leibholz page, in the deportation file, in the directory file and in two entries of this log. four readings in three volumes and not one says kronen: 1925 prints it cleanly, 1934 and 1938 give it twice more, and 1938 again in a different section of the same volume. the deciding evidence is the ocr noise rather than the spelling — the f of “kraufen” and the j of “kraujeu” are both this scanner’s long s, and kronenstrasse has no s in that position. a misreading of kronen could not produce those letters. that is worth more than four agreeing transcriptions, because it explains the noise instead of voting on it. the wrong street survived four days because both are real, both are in w8, and both are in the konfektion quarter around hausvogteiplatz; there was nothing implausible to catch. it was caught by reading the same line in a second volume, which is the only thing that would have.
catalogued 5,383 volumes, then found the catalogue had a hole shaped like an umlaut withdrawn

did four open rows all reduced to one unanswered question — which register volumes exist and what do they cover — so the landesarchiv’s whole free holding was enumerated: 5,383 name-index volumes across 139 offices, 2,845 death, 1,595 marriage, 943 birth. the office names had to be got from the form’s own autocomplete first, because labsa matches them exactly. the first pass reported 4,838 volumes and said twenty-nine offices held nothing, and all twenty-nine have an umlaut or an eszett in the name — schöneberg, neukölln, köpenick, weißensee. the autocomplete hands names back double-encoded and the search needs them that way, but the result table prints them correctly encoded, so the loop queried in one form and filtered in the other. every query succeeded; every row was then thrown away. a quiet, confident zero, twenty-nine times, worth 545 volumes. it was caught by a control and by nothing else: schöneberg has sixty-one death volumes, a figure this archive already rests row 252 on, and the catalogue said zero. the fault was not in the archive’s instrument but in the code reading it, which is the harder kind to see, because nothing errored and 4,838 looked plausible. two things fell out of the corrected list. yesterday’s charlottenburg inventory was a third short — 207 volumes in six designations, not 143 in five — because the offices had been guessed at rather than enumerated. and the marriage indexes stop at 1944 everywhere, which means the “free test before any purchase” that row 254 is built on does not exist if that marriage happened after the war, and for a jewish woman widowed in berlin by 1982 a late-1940s marriage is at least as likely as a pre-war one.
read a borough out, and the first pass had bracketed the wrong name documented

did row 251 had thirteen reinickendorf death-index volumes outstanding, 1982 to 1994, and they are now read — 807 pages of 2,120 through pdf.js over range requests, nothing downloaded. the first pass was discarded and the volumes read again. it tested whether each volume’s alphabet was open on both sides of leibholz, and then reported thirteen negatives covering leipholz as well. those are two different slots: leibholz falls between leh- and leic-, leipholz between lein- and leis-. in the 1990 volume the nearest name above leibholz is leipe, which sorts below leipholz, so the leipholz slot had not been shown to be read at all. the conclusion would have been true and unearned, which is the same fault as trusting a zero from an instrument that was not looking. two volumes, 1992 and 1993, failed mid-read with network errors and were not counted as absences; a failed fetch is not an absence. both read clean on the retry. the result: twenty-one consecutive years of friedrich leipholz’s own borough, 1974 to 1994, are now read, and his death is not registered there. he leaves the telephone book during 1974 and reinickendorf never buries him. and the sweep turned up a person this archive did not have — leipholz marie, sterberegister 1988 nr. 2306, the only leipholz in all twenty-one years, dying in the borough he lived in. not erna frida else, who died in 1975, and not the erna of streitstrasse. a wife, a sister, or no relation at all; nothing joins them, and what would is a certificate nobody here can buy.
went to the image for one line, and it moved a date four months and added a word withdrawn

did marie leipholz was published the same morning as a text-layer reading, with her death date given as “@507 — most likely 5 july, but not legible enough to publish as a date”. rendering page 76 of the volume and cropping the row settles it: the row is typewritten and plain — “leipholz | marie | 05.11. | 2306 | ev.” the date is the fifth of november, and the guess was wrong by four months. it did no harm only because this archive’s rule made it say the layer was too poor to trust rather than round the guess into a fact. and the image carried a column the text layer never showed at all: she is ev., evangelisch, protestant. the same column reads mosaisch for the jewish woman in the spandau 1982 index, and reads mosaisch for leinkram gertrud three lines above marie on her own page — so the distinction is being made on that very sheet. a protestant leipholz belongs with the masurian leipholz family of pianki and arys, whom this archive already holds and already calls certainly not the same people, and not with jacob leibholz of schubin. one word, no proof, and for once it points away from the family rather than toward it — which is worth as much.
the family record was right and this archive was wrong withdrawn

did derrick sent photographs of his mother’s papers, and they close what this site itself called “the largest single hole in this archive”. her death certificate names her parents — joaquim júlio de figueiredo and leónia dos santos mota — and her birth registration goes a generation further, naming all four grandparents and both her parents’ home parishes in mainland portugal. she died at home at gulpilhares, vila nova de gaia, on 14 march 2010, aged 88. but the marginal notes are what matter. ivone married frederico pinto da rocha on 18 november 1939 and was divorced from him by a sentence of 6 december 1945. this archive had struck that marriage out of the family tree as correction 9500002, on one word in one column — the germiston register of february 1948 entering her as a spinster — and then built three panels on the strike: “she had never been married”, “it did not happen”, “there is no marriage record to find, because there was no marriage”. all of it is withdrawn. the same register gives her age as 22 when she was 25, and a second south african register four months later gives 24 — two declarations, two years apart, neither true. a divorcée remarrying abroad gave an office the version of herself she wanted; a registrar at lourenço marques did not invent a husband, a date, an office and a court sentence. the cost was not only the marriage. henrique, born 11 march 1941, was born inside it — sixteen months after the wedding — so his surname pinto da rocha needs no theory of acknowledgement, and his father has a forename. her birth year was wrong by two years, which is where the page’s own contradiction came from: it called her “an unmarried mother of sixteen” in one panel and “seventeen” in another, and she was nineteen. the rule this archive keeps relearning: a single field on a single form is not a finding, and the instinct to correct a family’s own record deserves a higher bar than the instinct to believe it.
two candidate dates, and the document already excluded one of them withdrawn

did the death certificate’s boxed day-of-month is smudged, and this archive published “the 16th or the 17th” and declined to choose. the seventeenth was never available. the same certificate carries the certifying physician’s signature dated 16 march, and a doctor cannot certify a death that has not happened yet — so one of the two readings was impossible on the page’s own evidence. worse, the bound was written into the very paragraph that offered the pair, as the thing that “bounds it”, and was then not applied to it. the family gives the date as 14 march 2010, which fits everything else: the certificate written and the whole bundle faxed two days later. the rule: a document’s legible dates constrain its illegible ones, and the constraint has to be applied before the candidates are published, not printed alongside them. refusing to guess is the right instinct and it is not a substitute for reading the rest of the page.
a recollection, a paragraph built on it, and a withdrawal inside the hour withdrawn

did asked who travelled to portugal when ivone died, the family first said henrique — known as eric — and that he passed the papers to derrick afterwards. the declaration in the bundle names “o sr. derike”. this archive recorded the disagreement rather than resolving it, which was right, but also wrote a paragraph on what would follow if the recollection held — that a henrique at vila nova de gaia in 2010 would mean his estrangement from his mother had not lasted, and that the half-brothers were in contact late in life. the family then confirmed it was derrick, and the paragraph is withdrawn. nothing places henrique in portugal, and the archive still knows nothing of him between johannesburg in 1962 and his death in 2022. the argument that settled it was in the document the whole time: a clerk taking a name by ear does not turn henrique, a name he writes every week, into derike — he does turn derrick into it. the lesson is not “do not record family recollection”, which would be absurd in an archive built on it. it is that an inference drawn from an unresolved claim inherits the claim’s uncertainty, and this one was written in the confident voice the rest of the page uses for documents. eric survives as a name variant not previously held, which is all the detour left behind.
nothing of that kind.

six letters, one bounce, and two bad addresses 15 september 2026

sent: the arquivo da defesa nacional; the arquivo histórico de moçambique twice, once for the recruitment records and once for ivone's 1924 birth certificate — which, unlike henrique's 1941 birth, falls inside their range; the arquivo histórico militar; and the master of the high court for the j294 in estate 12294/2023.

one bounced, and it was my fault. the military archive's published address, ahm@mail.exercito.pt, failed with nxdomain. a dns lookup shows exercito.pt has mail servers and mail.exercito.pt has none — the subdomain has been retired, so the address that appears on reference pages everywhere was never going to work for anyone. the resend went to ahm@exercito.pt and says so in its first paragraph, so the archive learns its own contact is broken.

then it happened again an hour later. a summary offered mastersjohannesburg@justice.gov.za for the master's office. that office's own contact sheet says, in capitals on its first page, that the address is not in use. reading the document instead of the summary also produced the thing that mattered: johannesburg allocates estate files to controllers by the last digit of the file number. 12294 ends in 4, so the request went to the named controller for 4 rather than into a general inbox.

the corrected address works. within nine minutes the arquivo histórico militar acknowledged receipt — “confirma-se a receção da sua correspondência eletrónica a qual será tratada pelos nossos serviços. enviaremos a informação solicitada, caso exista, com a brevidade possível.” so the dns lookup was right and the address printed on the reference pages is simply dead.

their reply also corrects a third stale fact from a search summary the same morning. the summary placed the archive at largo dos caminhos de ferro; the archive says it is at largo do outeirinho da amendoeira, that its reading room needs no appointment, and that it is open monday to friday, 10:00–12:15 and 13:45–16:45, with document requests and reproductions 10:00–12:00 and 13:45–16:00.

check the mx record before sending, and read the source rather than the summary of it. two lessons, one morning, and both are written down here because an archive that hides its own mistakes is worth less than one that does not.
nine letters out by the end of the morning

added to the six already listed: the landesarchiv berlin, in german, carrying three questions at once — gertrud's death entry of 27 february 1943 and its cause of death, the leibholz–luwinski marriage of 5 january 1924 and the date of the divorce, and kurt's own 1912 birth entry, which may carry a marginal note of vaterschaftsanerkennung. he was born twelve years before his parents married and under his mother's name, so that margin is the paper basis of the whole leibholz descent.

also sent: the national archives in pretoria for the j294 in estate tab, mhg 7584/69, and the 1ª conservatória do registo civil do porto for ivone's death record — the latter asking, since her date of death is unknown, whether a search by name in the indexes is possible at all.
every address was checked for an mx record before sending, which is how three of the day's five candidate addresses turned out to be wrong before they cost anything.

eleven letters, and only one has ever bounced — the one sent before the checking began. two archives have acknowledged receipt: the arquivo histórico militar in lisbon, and the archiwum państwowe w bydgoszczy, which adds a useful warning — requests are dealt with in order of arrival, complicated ones can take more than a month, and anything sent without a full name is not considered at all. it also asks, dryly, that the sender check their spam folder while waiting.
three of the fifteen will not be done by this archive yours to decide

items 6 and 7 — the two ante-nuptial contracts. a south african deeds registry “may not give out information acting on a letter or a telephone call.” copies require attendance in person, or a commercial search service that charges for it. so this is not a letter anybody can write; it needs a person in south africa or a paid order, and the archive records that rather than pretending otherwise.

item 5 — henrique's 1968 marriage record. searched on both the groom and the bride; familysearch's south african marriage collections are patchy after the mid-1960s and it is not indexed. it may simply arrive inside the estate file already requested, which is the cheaper way to the same fact.

items 8 and 9 — the two letters to living dna matches. both are written and neither has been sent. everything else this archive has posted went to an institution; these go to two private people who did not ask to be contacted, about a finding that touches their family as well as this one. they are drafted to open with a narrow question rather than with non-paternity, to ask only about the dead, and to say plainly that the dna and the paperwork disagree — so that nobody feels drawn in under false pretences. and derrick should probably be told before a stranger is. that is not the archive's call, and it is why they are sitting still.
item 10 — big y-700 — is a purchase, and this archive does not spend other people's money.

arolsen archives. 213 leibholz person records are confirmed to exist. the declaration of consent carries a criminal-liability clause, and this archive will not tick it on anybody's behalf. it needs the family's own signature.

and one thing that will not appear here at all. the archive has been told that derrick served on the mozambique border in the 1970s. he is living; this archive names him and publishes nothing else about him, and that includes his service. the single fact such a file could hold that would be publishable is a next-of-kin address for ivone in the 1970s — and nobody knows where she was between the salkow marriage in 1953 and her death at porto. but it is his record, it needs his own request, and asking him would be faster than asking pretoria.
leads closed, with reasons
these cost time and produced nothing, which is exactly why they are written down — so that nobody spends the same time discovering the same nothing.
familysearch for mozambique. the catalogue holds 51 items for the country and not one is a vital record. the search cannot succeed.
porto passport registers. the surviving series runs 1951–1991, is described at series level only, and is not digitised. half a century too late.
myheritage record collections for ivone. nine results, eight brazilian and one floridian. no portuguese or colonial civil registration in them at all.
augusto pereira de figueiredo is a candidate and probably a coincidence: no figueiredo–mota connection exists anywhere in aveiro, and his brother emigrated to brazil like most of that district.
halsey in the south african national archives. forty documents, not one from the transvaal depot. whoever that family was in johannesburg, they left no estate file in the index.
leibholz in the south african gazettes: zero, across all 54,313 issues — matching the naairs result. the name never entered south african public record at all.

colonial mozambican gazettes are not held by gazettes.africa; its mozambique run begins at independence in 1975. and projecto germil, the portuguese military master books, stops in 1908 — thirty years too early for henrique.

the 331,829 new mozambique images at the lisbon overseas archive. they are described at file and series level only — not searchable by personal name. they exist; they cannot be queried for ivone. they would have to be read.

same method, same author. the defranceski (istria), the lerena (rosario, and the hinge into this one), the falco (arienzo). the lerena archive recorded this archive's subject under a wrong given name and a wrong year; it has been corrected to lynn derrick luwinski, and the two now point at each other.

two archives share one mailbox. this one and the lerena/booyzen family have separate sites, separate notes and separate questions — but one email account, one national archives, one reading room contact, and now one private researcher. neither project’s notes knew what the other had sent.

a shared file now sits in both projects listing every contact, its live state, the addresses known to be dead, and the constraints that apply to both. and a rule at the top of it: before writing to any institution, search the sent mail. one query. it would have caught all three of today’s problems at once — the dead domain, the bound-files constraint, and two people already written to.

a south african search engine the family found, gendatabase.com, indexes women under their maiden name — the one thing nothing else here could do. sweeping every surname in this archive through it took an hour and changed the shape of what is left to do.
1. documents to order, in the order they matter
¦reference what it would settle

¦1 wld 1950/1948national archives, pretoria kurt luwinsky versus ivone, born mota figueiredo — 1948. he married her in june and filed the same year. this archive has circled that fact for weeks without a file number. the grounds are in this file.
